    • Google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI.
    • Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me.
    • Recent findings suggest that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google likes to use your conversations with Gemini for model training to help improve the AI. But for people with privacy concerns, the only way to opt out of this was to delete your entire chat history. Now, Google is overhauling the process to eliminate that drawback.

    Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me.

    Recent findings suggest that in a change set to roll out in the coming weeks, you’ll be able to put the brakes on Gemini model training without losing access to your previous conversations with the AI. Here’s how this works now — and how it will work down the road.

    It has been revealed that right now, Gemini offers a setting called Keep Activity that controls not only whether and for how long your chats are saved but also whether they’re used to train the AI. You can’t separate the two.

    In a recent development, to correct this problem, Google will replace Keep Activity with two new settings. With the first setting, you’ll be able to keep or delete your past chats and choose how long your history will be saved. With the second setting, you’ll be able to decide whether your chats, including all text and attachments, will be used for model training.

    Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

    “With this change, you will be able to keep your history while independently controlling generative AI model training,” Google said in an announcement shared to Gemini users via email.

    Here’s how this will play out. If your Keep Activity setting is off when this change is made, both fresh settings will be off. If your Keep Activity setting is on, both new settings will be on. That means you’ll need to head to Gemini’s Settings if you wish to opt out of model training but still be able to view and access your previous chats.

    In a recent development, almost all AIs include a setting for model training that you typically have to manually disable if you’re concerned about your privacy. But most let you opt out without turning off your chat history.

    ChatGPT offers a setting called “Improve the model for everyone,” which is double-speak for model training. But this is easy enough to turn off. Microsoft Copilot provides settings for “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations,” both of which you can disable to opt out of model training. Claude’s AI training option is turned off by default. But you can always control this by checking the setting for “Help improve our AI models.”.

    Also: 5 ways AI will change how you defend your business in 2027.

    It has been revealed that in all those cases, you still retain access to your conversation history. In contrast, Google has been the only AI player among the majors to impose a restriction for those who want to opt out of AI training. Based on past actions, Google has often earned a reputation for being privacy-unfriendly. I’m glad to see the company take this step in the right direction.

    #27920. Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (912 w)

    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Apple’s Support Community Shuts Down on Friday, Removing User Discussions

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (912 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations.
    • According to recent reports, A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov.
    • Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Apple’s Support Communities website will shut down permanently on Friday, removing decades of Apple owner conversations. For a few more hours, the website will remain read-only, but I’ve found the search function crashes intermittently, so even that ability isn’t very reliable.

    According to recent reports, A notification on the community forum appeared on Nov. 10, warning visitors that the site would shut down and be offline entirely on Friday. If you want to look up a specific Apple troubleshooting topic on iPhones or HomePods, you should do it this evening. Soon, the entire peer advice and support site, which has been operating for nearly three decades, will be gone.

    Apple was a pioneer in community support forums before the aughts, letting people discuss their Mac issues as early as 1998. For those of you who might remember, that’s the year Apple debuted its iMac G3, the desktop with a translucent blue teardrop-shaped case. The iMac G3 abandoned legacy ports and the floppy disc drive in favor of CD-ROM and USB.

    Sources indicate that back then, the site was called Apple Tech Exchange, later renamed Apple Discussions until it eventually became the Apple Support Community in 2011. Many still turned to forums for DIY solutions, using it to get advice from other tinkerers interested in figuring out how to fix things on their own.

    An Apple spokesperson told CNET the decision was made “after careful evaluation of our strategy and our customers’ needs.” Apple’s site notification directs people to visit the official Apple Support site. You’ll also be able to use Apple’s online chat, support phone numbers and in-store support, the same way they worked in the past.

    Apple is one of the first American tech companies to give up its community discussion site — Google still has Google Communities Help, and Amazon manages its own forum domain with discussions from both staff and owners. But Apple’s sudden closure could indicate a major shift, with others eventually following suit. It has highlighted an ongoing discussion about the role of peer support in tech, how AI has changed our online conversations and more.

    When news of the shutdown spread, Apple users flocked to the internet to express everything from dismay to vindication.

    In a recent development, for many, the Apple Support Community forums were controversial, not least because it wasn’t always clear how they worked. The site contained “user-submitted content, comments and opinions” and was “for informational purposes only,” yet many would mistake it for official Apple Support from staff.

    In discussions on Reddit about the closure, many bemoaned the absence of real Apple employees from the site’s forums and found the advice from other Support Community users to often be frustrating and not worth the effort. On the unofficial Apple subreddit, many mourned the loss of community while also noting that answers on the forum were often much harder to come by. Others remarked the site grew less helpful over the years.

    CNET phone reviewer and senior editor Mike Sorrentino told me that the forum shutdown “will likely drive customers looking for help with basic questions to Apple’s official support articles rather than user-created threads.” But Sorrentino also acknowledged that the move reflects a general trend away from the site, with more people getting answers from sites like Reddit. “Apple’s always been big on controlling what information is shown on its website, and in that view, moving away from user discussion makes sense,” he mentioned.

    Just this week, I used the Apple Support Community site when looking for an answer to a problem implementing Apple Intelligence on my home security cameras, which required jumping through multiple hoops. Perhaps tellingly, I ended up finding the correct answer on Reddit. But that could become harder to do in the near future.

    Industry observers note that the shutdown of Apple’s peer support forums is definitely a sign of the times, especially as tech companies push users away from repairing their own devices and toward replacing them outright — or at least encourage device owners to pay for official support services. It’s also a sign of the growing role of artificial intelligence, which is capitalizing on user-created content to provide summaries, moving people away from organic discussion and exchange on sites like these.

    In a recent development, reddit has lucrative data-licensing contracts with Google and OpenAI, allowing the companies to train their AI models on Reddit’s massive archive of human discussions, as well as surface Reddit content in tools like Google AI Overviews and ChatGPT. Reddit is also moving to a login-only viewing mode, making it significantly harder for casual people to find answers unless they trust AI summaries.

    Industry observers note that apple may be leery of keeping so much user knowledge online for AI models to scrape for their own answers. The company may also want to prevent AI summaries from providing information from past forum owners on how to jailbreak Apple devices or DIY fixes, even as the EU has mandated that Apple start building replaceable batteries by next year. And it wouldn’t be a good look if Siri AI started regurgitating incorrect or outdated info it had picked up from Apple’s own sites.

    In a recent development, whatever the reason, the circle of Apple customers helping users has grown smaller, and that doesn’t bode well for support forums as a whole. It may be time to start archiving those years of data before other tech companies implement similar plans.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 upgrade for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of upcoming features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.
    • While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.
    • The best laptop for Android consumers is something else.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    On Monday, Google rolled out an M157 upgrade for the Chrome web browser on Googlebook OS, with a handful of upcoming features and performance boosts to streamline your workflow and browsing experience.

    While the first Googlebooks on the market have received mixed reviews, these features could help the laptops gain more useful features in Chrome that other browsers already offer.

    Also: Googlebooks? The best laptop for Android consumers is something else.

    Here are the five new Chrome features on Googlebook OS to know about.

    According to recent reports, if you’ve ever had to share your screen on a video call, you know how irritating it can be to switch tabs without having to repeatedly start and stop sharing. This Chrome update adds a tab-sharing controls bar; when you share a browser tab in a video call, Chrome will display a persistent control bar at the top of the window so you can “Stop sharing” or “Share this tab instead” from any tab.

    Also: 6 Chrome default settings I changed to instantly.

    When you hover over a collapsed vertical tab rail with your mouse or trackpad, it will expand, so you can read full tab titles, switch tabs, or manage groups. The rail will collapse again when you move the cursor away.

    In a recent development, this auto-expand feature is enabled by default. If you want to turn it off or on, go to Settings > Appearance > Tab position > “Auto expand tabs on hover,” or right-click the vertical tab rail.

    Sources indicate that the Chrome update allows you to manually resize your vertical tab bar to view longer page titles when needed. The browser will remember your custom tab width, even after you open a fresh window or restart the browser. (You’ll just need to turn “Auto expand tabs on hover” off for it to work.).

    You can now save individual Chrome Settings subpages as direct web addresses that you can type, bookmark, or link to directly (for example, chrome://settings/privacy), meaning you won’t have to go digging around in menus to change your preferences anymore. You can navigate between these Settings subpages with the Back and Forward buttons.

    Industry observers note that the system’s “Save As” file picker is now enabled by default for menu save actions, such as “Save link as” and “Save image as,” so you can more easily rename files and select a destination folder. This includes Google Drive or external storage.

    It has been revealed that also: Google Chrome running slow? 5 easy ways to speed it up fast.

    Outside of these upcoming features, a few of Chrome M157’s performance fixes include the ability to press Ctrl+L to reveal and select web addresses; keeping your bookmarks bar visible in fullscreen mode and while screen sharing; better media controls while using Picture-in-Picture mode; and the ability to partially translate PDFs within your browser.

    If you have Chrome set up to automatically download and install updates, you won’t have to lift a finger to take advantage of the newly introduced features and performance boosts.

    But if you’ve disabled automatic updates, you can manually revision by selecting the three-dot menu in the top-right corner of your Chrome window and navigating to Help > About Google Chrome > Relaunch.

    Also: My week with latest Googlebooks: The good, the bad, and the promising.

    Recent findings suggest that if the Relaunch option is greyed out or nowhere to be found, you’re running on the latest version of Chrome. And if you were working on something before the upgrade, don’t worry: Chrome will save your open tabs and reopen them automatically when you restart.

    Google has unveiled that it’s turning Gems, a Gemini feature that lets you create customizable AI chatbots, into Skills, which let you create custom instructions for Gemini. Any Gems you have created will automatically convert, but you can transfer them manually if you want to start using them now.

    To help with the transition, Google revealed that two Gems features are moving, too: the ability to share creations and to include Drive, Notebook, and Photos files as part of your Skill’s instructions.

    While the Gemini Gems feature is technically going away, any Gems you’ve created aren’t.

    If you access the Gems portion of Gemini (since the feature is on the way out, you now have to access this through Settings), you’ll see a message that claims “Starting November 17, 2026, we’ll automatically begin migrating all of your Gems to Skills.” (The cutoff date for accessing your Gems will be Dec. 16, 2026. Workspace business, enterprise, and non-profit accounts will get cut off in March 2027, and Workspace education accounts will be cut off in June 2027.).

    According to recent reports, A Gemini Skill functions much the same as a Gem. You describe specific situations when Gemini should use the Skill automatically and tell Gemini what you want the Skill to do (it’s best to give specific examples of output). Google gives the example of a marketing team sharing a brand-voice skill that references their brand guidelines doc in Drive, or a team lead sharing an onboarding skill based on the team handbook.

    The biggest difference is that Gems were standalone chats, while Skills are custom instructions that work in any conversation.

    You can create as many Skills as you want, but only 100 can be active at a time.

    To get users familiar with Skills, Google is bringing over two features from Gems.

    It has been revealed that first, you can now share any Skill with other owners. When you share a Skill, you can choose whether the other person has permission to edit or view only. To share a Skill, go to the three-bar menu in the top left > Customize > Skills. You can view or change permissions from that screen.

    Also: I checked Gemini’s new Memory summary to see what it knew about me – how to see and edit yours.

    When a Skill is added, Gemini can use it automatically, or you can @mention it in chat to trigger it. One small caveat, though: you can only share Skills through the Gemini web app at the moment, not the mobile app.

    Additionally, when you’re creating a Gemini Skill, you can choose to include files of up to 100MB from other Google products like Drive, Photos, and Notebook, along with files from your local device. Gemini will reference these files every time the Skill runs and patch in real time, Google notes. These features existed with Gems; Google is just moving them to Skills to make the new feature more comparable.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids.
    • Recent findings suggest that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin.
    • Sources indicate that on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Uber, the popular ridesharing app, is testing rides for kids. Uber Kids will cater to youngsters ages 10 to 12, those awkward years before adolescence. The fresh program expands on the tech giant’s other offering to underage passengers, Uber Teens, which debuted in 2023 and provides rides to teenagers ages 13 to 17 in select cities.

    Recent findings suggest that the pilot program for Uber Kids starts in three US cities for a limited time: Austin, Texas; Nashville, Tennessee; and Madison, Wisconsin. Its expansion will depend on how well it performs in those regions. If successful, Uber Kids could bring a whole newly introduced influx of customers to the app, specifically parents and families needing help getting their kids from point A to point B.

    Sources indicate that on the surface, it feels like a questionable proposition, given all the potential harms and dangers to young people traveling alone with a stranger. But it seems like Uber took those concerns into account. The rideshare app has added a slew of mandatory requirements for both approved guardians and qualified drivers.

    Recent findings suggest that first off, kids won’t simply be able to order a ride for themselves. The adult user must add the child to their family profile and complete an onboarding session covering the service’s safety features. They’ll also need to set up PIN verification for every trip. The parent or guardian must be present at the pickup location and provide the driver with a note containing the drop-off instructions.

    As any parent would likely wonder (myself included), what about the drivers? How are they vetted?

    According to Uber, only the highest-rated drivers will be invited to take part in the program. They’ll need to pass thorough background checks and successfully complete an Uber Kids education curriculum. Moreover, they must agree to use live video streaming in their cars so that parents and guardians can watch the trip every step of the way.

    According to recent reports, live videos of underage passengers bring up a bunch of potential red flags, but Uber states all recordings will be encrypted, and no driver will have access to the content. Furthermore, sensors and GPS data will track the ride if the trip is interrupted or veers off course.

    Recent findings suggest that uber could face a tough time recruiting drivers for Uber Kids. Transporting minors adds extra responsibility and requires specific skills that many drivers may want to avoid. To sweeten the deal, Uber is offering eligible drivers a $20 bonus on their first ride and an extra $7 per trip after that.

    An Uber spokesperson didn’t immediately reply to our request for comment.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the manufacturer introduced two latest frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks.
    • Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.
    • Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    At today’s Microsoft Ignite 2026 keynote, the manufacturer introduced two latest frontier AI models built for what the company describes as “everyday” coding tasks. But there’s a bigger story: what these models might mean for Microsoft’s AI costs and its dependence on OpenAI.

    Microsoft claims its MAI Code 2 model shows 96% of Claude Opus 5.5 performance at 5% of Opus 5.5’s price.

    Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

    In a recent development, microsoft states MAI Code 2 offers comparable performance to GPT-6.1 Sol or Opus 5.5 at a fraction of the cost. Microsoft’s Code 2 Flash model is comparable to the lower-end GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, also at considerably lower cost.

    This doesn’t mean that those of us who pay for $100/month subscriptions will suddenly get the equivalent for five bucks. Instead, these are usage-based metrics based on API usage.

    According to recent reports, it’s also important to understand that the benchmarks are all Microsoft-provided. Performance numbers may well differ once the models undergo independent performance tests.

    Throughout Satya Nadella’s keynote, Microsoft highlighted slides referencing a wide range of foundation models that are intended to work with Copilot and other Microsoft offerings. Microsoft famously has a multi-billion-dollar investment in OpenAI dating back to 2023, and has built many of its products and services around OpenAI intellectual property.

    But now, Redmond is benchmarking its internally built models against Anthropic and OpenAI offerings, and also touting that it’s integrating these new models as optional choices for GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365, and Fabric.

    Also: 75% of developers I surveyed prefer Claude Code over Codex.

    Industry observers note that one thing that Nadella made clear in today’s keynote is how central AI is becoming in everything Microsoft does. Nearly all of those AI operations previously involved the company paying some token fees back to the frontier model providers or customers doing the same thing.

    But with high-performing models of its own, Microsoft may become substantially less dependent on outside model providers, especially for the incredible volume of fairly basic and routine AI requests that occur across the company’s vast product line.

    It has been revealed that if you think back over the history of agentic work models like ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork, you may recall that they originated as agentic coding tools. As customers adopted the coding harnesses in Claude Code and OpenAI Codex to off-label productivity applications, the AI companies noticed and packaged work-centric agentic tools that were more non-programmer-friendly.

    Also: I let ChatGPT Work and Claude Cowork loose on my files – only one made me nervous.

    According to recent reports, there’s a lot of similarity between a coding agent and a work agent, including understanding a complex environment, using tools to change things, and producing reliable results. Coding turns out to be a very good environment for developing and testing these capabilities, particularly because code output is highly measurable. Coding agents are effective training grounds for non-coding work agents.

    Industry observers note that this becomes really interesting in today’s announcement. Along with Code 2 and Code 2 Flash, Microsoft declared MAI Work Flash, which it describes as having been derived from Code 2 Flash. Work Flash can help generate formulas in Excel, work with documents and instructions in Word, track decisions and extract useful information from Teams, and more.

    In a recent development, think about the level of intelligence these tasks are demanding from the AI models. Not that much. As long as the models are good enough, they’ll be good enough.

    If Microsoft can reduce its expenses and use reliable models at a much lower price, the company itself will be able to save quite a bit of money across its entire software economy, while at the same time maintaining a deeper level of vertical integration and, therefore, control.

    Industry observers note that let’s run some hypothetical numbers. Let’s say a organization is spending $0.01 per AI request, which, with these new models, can drop down to $0.001 per request.

    Also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer very carefully first.

    A company with a daily inference cost of a million dollars (a company like Microsoft, for example) could drop that daily cost to about $100,000. Add that up across a year, and the change in models could save $325 million annually.

    In a recent development, A million here, a million there. Pretty soon, you’re talking real money.

    Industry observers note that there’s no direct evidence that Microsoft is trying to produce replacement models for the frontier providers’ offerings. But it is an interesting and compelling story if we look at Microsoft developing its own engines for the software it sells.

    Recent findings suggest that microsoft says the numbers it’s reporting at are using a 50% introductory discount. That’s why I measured against $0.001 per request instead of $0.0005 per request above.

    It has been revealed that benchmark selection could be cherry-picking. The numbers are impressive. But as we all know, there are lies, damned lies, and benchmark results. I’m fairly sure Microsoft isn’t padding these numbers too much, because it benefits from the new models more than even its own customers, but still. It’s an open issue.

    The manufacturer also described clearly that these upcoming models are not designed to handle the most challenging agentic and research workloads. You’re probably not going to use them to solve a decades-old mathematics challenge. But you’re very likely to use them to reformat your PowerPoint.

    Industry observers note that speaking of reformatting your PowerPoint, Microsoft also emphasized that these latest models did unusually well on visualization assignments. That’s a very good fit for not only UI design challenges but also graphics and slide production.

    By Jeremy Bowman – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    The torch in AI has been passed.

    In a recent development, it seems fitting in some ways that Anthropic's (ANT -8.50%) IPO came just a week after Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned as CEO, leaving the chipmaker in turmoil. Nvidia had been the stock market's avatar for AI since the launch of ChatGPT, but with Anthropic now becoming the first AI lab to go public, it's set to take over as the market's best reflection of AI sentiment.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic is a pure-play AI organization founded in 2021 by a group of former OpenAI employees who thought that company was too weak on safety. Anthropic builds AI models and software products based on its frontier intelligence platform, Claude.

    Sources indicate that anthropic's IPO also gave the tech giant a chance to have the investing world's full attention, and CEO Dario Amodei spoke for about five minutes at the Nasdaq stock exchange Thursday, sharing his vision for the company. Here are three things investors should know about the newly public company, direct from Amodei.

    Dario Amodei. Image source: Getty Images.

    Anthropic has made its prioritization of safety clear from its inception, and AI safety has only become more salient amid concerns of AI models going rogue, escaping sandboxes, and the intensifying competition with China.

    Anthropic's emphasis on safety may also be a competitive advantage at a time when AI is facing a backlash. The midterm elections reflected growing discontent with data centers and could lead to a slowdown or increased restrictions on them, at least in some states.

    The emphasis on safety also acts in the company's interest in terms of liability and reputational damage, as the future of AI is wide open and will be determined by companies like Anthropic.

    Amodei told the audience, "There's a gigantic difference between how AI will go if we pay little attention to safety versus how it will go if we are obsessed with safety, and an obsession with safety and public benefit has been built into Anthropic's DNA from the start.".

    Amodei wants everyone, including investors, owners, and AI skeptics, to know that he's one of the good guys.

    In a similar vein, Amodei described a best-case scenario for the AI competition as a "race to the top.".

    Amodei said, "If we can show it's possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others will be inspired to do the same.".

    Recent findings suggest that if that spirit takes hold in the industry, then, he said, everybody wins, no matter who has the best models. Amodei assured investors that they intend to lead that race, saying, "The race to the top works best when driven from the front of the pack, and we fully hope and expect to do so, but the goal is to make the whole industry better, regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time.".

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Amodei began his comments with a story about how his father died of a disease, Hepatitis C, that was cured just a few years later.

    The event clearly indicated Amodei the power of invention and new technology, and after beginning his career in biology, he moved over to artificial intelligence, where he sees the potential for tremendous breakthroughs in medicine and beyond.

    The departure of Jensen Huang due to a scandal involving multiple affairs is a reminder of the importance of character in leadership, and Amodei seems to possess that sufficiently.

    It has been revealed that anthropic is a mission-driven tech giant and the rare public benefit corporation on the stock market. Amodei brings a deep commitment to that mission and a personal passion for research and intelligence that can cure diseases and solve humanity's most pressing problems.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    As smart home and home security devices become more common, we’ve all got more devices around our homes when guests come over. Since I test home security and multiple smart devices, I tend to have a lot. But they don’t have to be a distraction when you have visitors staying over. On the contrary, smart tech can usually help out.

    If you have holiday or event looks involving guests, especially guests staying over a day or two, I highly suggest making these adjustments to your smart home devices. These changes save me headaches and time, while impressing guests. You may even decide to enable some features year-round.

    Read more: The 7 Most Common Home Security Mistakes to Stop Making.

    Doorbell chimes are just the start of your smart guest experience.

    According to recent reports, video doorbells often come with a feature in settings to switch to seasonal themes, including a variety of holiday sounds for the end of the year. Vivint is particularly good at this, equipping its video doorbell with options for many different holiday songs. Google Nest doorbells and Eufy doorbells also have holiday options.

    Smart lighting is easy to set up for certain times of day, dimming and brightening as necessary.

    According to recent reports, cameras and guests don’t play well together. Help everyone feel safe by pulling down the shutters on your indoor cameras, nanny cams and smart displays (or disabling them through settings, etc.). Let everyone know their privacy is secured while staying over. Video doorbells and outdoor cams are fine to leave functioning, especially if you want to keep an eye on kids going crazy in your backyard.

    Today’s smart lights include options to turn on at certain times of day or at sunrise, and at a specific brightness (and even color temperature). Some even allow you to gradually increase the brightness over an hour or so. Use these settings to set a simulated sunrise in key spots of the house to encourage guests to rise and shine at the right times. It’s especially handy if everyone needs to be up in the morning for a special activity — but make sure to provide coffee too.

    Aqara’s app distills a whole lot of smart lock options into a highly digestible product card.

    A smart lock allows for all kinds of tricks, like remote operation and auto-locking if it’s left unlocked. Those work great when you have guests over, but if you want to add even more options, many locks allow you to create temporary passes — including through common apps like Apple Home — and send them to your guest’s phones. That way they can come and go on their own schedules, and the door stays locked when no one is using it.

    Today’s smart thermostats, including the Google Nest, have humidity sensors, too.

    According to recent reports, keeping the thermostat triggering temperatures a bit low in winter is a great way to save energy, but not always the sign of a good host. Consider heading into your thermostat app and bumping up temperatures a few degrees, especially at night and the middle of the day, so everyone stays comfortable. The latest models can even sense humidity, which can be crucial if guests are sensitive to very dry or very wet air.

    ADT’s latest hub has a few extra tricks.

    In a recent development, home security system schedules usually call for arming the system during the day after everyone has left the house. That doesn’t work so well over the holidays, especially if you have guests over. Instead of disabling individual sensors, we suggest setting your home security system to disarm during the day.

    You can still get important alerts from devices like leak detectors or package-recognizing video doorbells with the system disarmed. And you can leave the night mode armed (which usually lets people move around but monitors doors and windows closely).

    A guest Wi-Fi network is an excellent add-on if you have multiple people coming to visit. It lets you set a separate network and easy-to-remember password for all guest devices, keeping your home network safer and letting you prioritize key home devices. Plus, you can keep reusing it whenever people come over in the future. We’ve got a full guide on how to set a guest network up, but it’s usually very easy with app settings.

    Prep your smart speakers for guests to avoid any problems.

    According to recent reports, smart home speakers like an Echo or the new Apple HomeView are excellent devices for playing holiday music for a whole house. But there’s a small problem: With a lot of extra guest devices on your Wi-Fi, music streaming may not be reliable. You can solve this problem by downloading a playlist to a device like a phone or tablet and playing it on the smart speaker via Bluetooth. Many common apps like Spotify let you do this, especially if you have a subscription.

    Voice assistants are handy and fun, but they can be a distraction when others are around, especially if kids start getting creative in their commands. You could turn voice assistants off entirely, but we like the option to limit what they can do.

    Sources indicate that for example, Alexa has a Voice ID section in its settings that allows you to limit skills and third-party services from working with any voice except the profiles you create and add for you and direct family members. Google Assistant has a very similar option with its Voice Match settings, which limits device controls to only certain voices.

    It’s also a good idea to set up a voice code to confirm any purchases made over voice assistants, so people can’t buy something with just a command.

    A wireless charger nearly anyone can use.

    With the ubiquitous Qi charging standard, wireless chargers can work with nearly any phone. Make things easier for your guests by setting out a wireless charger or two for them to use without managing a tangle of power adapters. Bonus points if you offer chargers that have multiple charging pads, sparing your outlets even more.

    Industry observers note that if you have a little extra time, most home security systems can connect to compatible smart lighting and let you create routines to make them more useful. Specifically, we’ve had great results creating night mode routines for security sensors that turn on nearby smart bulbs at low brightness settings when motion is detected.

    This way, if someone gets up in the middle of the night, they can have a soft light to help them find their way without disturbing anyone else.

    Recent findings suggest that don’t have a home security system? You don’t need one: Devices like this $50 Philips Hue motion sensor work independently and can automatically tell smart lights what to do when someone approaches.

    For more on protecting and utilizing your smart home, take a look at our favorite DIY home security systems, our list of the best smart home devices and our total smart home cheat sheet for all platforms.

    📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (791 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (791 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that we all know AI can get expensive.
    • Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
    • Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that we all know AI can get expensive. But does that expense result in real business value? That’s the trillion-dollar question Microsoft aims to answer with today’s introduction of Agent 365 Business Analytics.

    Also: Microsoft says its new AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

    Earlier this year, Microsoft introduced Agent 365, its tool for tracking agents the way an HR department would normally track human employees. With Agent 365 Business Analytics, Microsoft is attempting to build an accounting system for AI labor. The system attempts to calculate the economic value of the work performed by agents compared with what the agents cost, and then provide a return on investment estimate.

    Industry observers note that if it works, this is some very cool stuff. Microsoft is trying to map labor-market economics onto AI usage data to create value estimates.

    Also: Work IQ is Microsoft’s massive bet on agent-first enterprise IT, and I have questions.

    To do so, it uses real labor-costing information, including data from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, the O*NET database from the US Department of Labor, and its own LinkedIn Occupational Graph.

    This data, along with data gathered from Agent 365, is aggregated into analysis intended to answer:.

    The goal is to provide a comprehensive picture of AI spend against value produced.

    Software accounting is long established and straightforward. We measure subscription fees, cost per seat, compute costs, burden costs (like floor space and other infrastructure), and more. But AI work doesn’t fit that model, making it very hard to quantify value.

    According to recent reports, instead, Agent 365 Business Analytics measures cost both relative to human labor and in terms of technological expense. For example, it might look at a task and determine how much human effort that task would normally take, and then price that effort based on prevailing common labor rates.

    Industry observers note that then, it might factor in how much of the task was actually done by a human vs. how much was contributed by an AI, along with the estimated value of the AI’s contribution. Then it mixes in the actual AI processing cost (whether in subscriptions, tokens, on-premises infrastructure, and cloud support).

    Also: These Claude Enterprise features let you track AI ROI – what’s fresh.

    Sources indicate that what comes out is a hybrid labor estimate that combines human contribution, human-replacement savings, AI costs, and then potentially AI savings over human costs. It sounds positively Orwellian. But the bottom line is that companies really haven’t been able to understand the AI bottom line.

    There’s a catch. All these numbers are estimates. In its blog post, Redmond specifically claims, “Assisted hours are a directional estimate of work AI helped complete, not measured time saved or financial return.”.

    Recent findings suggest that in other words, what Agent 365 Business Analytics estimates might not actually line up with real-world experience or expenses. It’s also possible that AI work might have been assigned because there was AI to do the work, not that the AI was saving firm labor costs with every token processed.

    In other words, Microsoft may be able to tell you the economic value of AI-assisted work, but it can’t demonstrate definitively that the manufacturer saved any real money.

    Also: 5 reasons your organization needs a chief AI officer in 2026.

    I find it particularly telling that this is from the manufacturer that makes PowerPoint. Because now, with Agent 365 Business Analytics, it’s entirely possible that you could produce economic dashboards that look really, really impressive, but are entirely irrelevant to real life.

    It has been revealed that that’s not to say the product is useless. But it does go to the idea that you will have to be quite disciplined in how you interpret the results and how much stock you put in them for decision-making. It is one source of possible truth, not the source of absolute truth.

    According to recent reports, microsoft has been investing for decades to build out the core infrastructure of enterprise computing. AI isn’t any different when it comes to the company’s overall mission.

    With Agent 365 and the company’s related offerings, Microsoft wants to help you:.

    It has been revealed that this means the organization doesn’t necessarily have to provide you with the AI model to help you run your enterprise. With integration with offerings from OpenAI, Anthropic, Salesforce, Google, Databricks, Snowflake, and others, the company doesn’t even have to provide the apps or SaaS capabilities.

    But if it can get in there and manage your plumbing, help you control costs, and be the HR operation for your AI workforce, Microsoft could own a central piece of your business’s operations.

    #27903. Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (898 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Polaroid’s Portable Printer Got Me Right Back Into Journaling

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that I loved journaling as a child.
    • I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success.
    • Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that I loved journaling as a child. It helped me survive hormonal changes, the usual teen dramas, plus a hefty dose of existential angst. Then college called, and I moved to a different country, leaving behind my childhood, my Nirvana cassettes (I’m old, OK?) and, sadly, my journaling habit.

    I made multiple attempts to return to journaling throughout the years, with varying success. I’ve delved into bullet journals under the pretense of improving my productivity, but I gave up when it became too much effort. I’ve invested in multiple notebooks and planners, only to eventually neglect them.

    Recently, however, I found a way for me to actually stick to the habit: a $110 Polaroid Hi-Print pocket printer.

    According to recent reports, it all began when I discovered the wondrous world of journaling TikTok. In short-form videos, creators would show off beautiful journal pages decorated with colored markers, stickers, washi tape and, yes, photos — specifically photos from portable printers because the prints are small enough to fit within the confines of a typical journal or planner. I really liked the idea of decking out my journal pages with photos of my everyday life. I knew I had to get one.

    Recent findings suggest that after a bit of research, I decided on a couple of criteria. First, I wanted the printer to be a dye sublimation printer rather than a ZINK (Zero Ink) printer. Dye sublimation printers essentially use heat to transfer dye onto the paper, while ZINK printers use a special paper that activates under heat with no ink required (hence the name). Dye sublimation prints tend to be higher quality because it transfers the dye in layers of cyan, magenta and yellow, followed by a protective coating.

    Second, I wanted the photo to be on sticky paper so that I didn’t have to mess around with glue to add these photos to my journal.

    Industry observers note that I found quite a number of dye sublimation pocket printers on the market, but the one that caught my eye immediately was the Polaroid Hi-Print 2×3 Generation 2 pocket printer. I fell in love with it the moment I saw it. The sleek white design, the Polaroid logo and that curved rainbow accent on the edge really sealed the deal for me. Call me a sucker for style, I guess.

    I purchased a Hi-Print 2×3 “starter set,” which includes the printer along with two 2×3 paper cartridges. Each cartridge has 10 photo sheets, and each sheet is made out of sticky back photo paper, which is exactly what I wanted. Both the Gen 2 and the prior Gen 1 are easy to find; the main difference is the newer one uses a USB-C charging port while the original uses the older Micro-USB port.

    Getting started with the printer is simple enough: Download the Polaroid Hi-Print app, pair the printer with your phone and you’re ready to go. The app is fairly easy to navigate. I like that it lets you arrange your photos in collages so you’re not limited to just one photo per sheet. You can also decorate your prints with colorful frames or decorations. The printer even offers a mosaic option that lets you print out one substantial image using multiple sheets.

    Industry observers note that since it’s a dye sublimation printer, the Hi-Print prints out photos in stages. It lays down the different colors in multiple passes (yellow in the first pass, magenta in the second pass, and so forth). Because of that, printing does take a while: around 60 seconds per photo.

    But I don’t mind the delay, as the resulting photo quality is superb. The colors are vibrant and the overall image is nice and sharp. The contrast could be a little better, but for a little pocket printer, the quality definitely exceeded my expectations.

    There are a few downsides, however. The obvious one is that photo cartridges can be pretty expensive. One pack of 20 sheets is around $17, though you can get it for $14 each if you buy the 5-pack. That’s still almost 70 cents per 2×3 print. If you use multiple prints, that can add up pretty rapidly.

    Sources indicate that another downside is that it doesn’t have a super long battery life. It only has a 620mAh battery, which Polaroid says will last up to 20 photo printing sessions. I only ever use this printer at home, so this isn’t a big deal for me, but I can see this being a potential disappointment if you want to bring this printer on the road. That noted, if you do want to charge it, it doesn’t take that long. Polaroid says it takes under an hour, and that feels about right based on my experience.

    I’ve had this printer for a few months now, and I’m very pleased with it. Since I use the photos primarily with my journal, I also really appreciate how thin the photo sheets are, so they don’t bulk up the pages too much. I truly enjoy printing out my little creations, cutting out my collages and then decorating my journal with them.

    I might not have my childhood back nor my Nirvana cassettes, but at least I’ve finally recaptured the joys of journaling — even if it did require a bit of help from a pocket printer.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:05PM EST.
    • Choosing between a steady staples giant and a premium apparel leader requires balancing reliability against growth potential.
    • According to recent reports, colgate-Palmolive dominates everyday essentials like toothpaste and pet nutrition, while Lululemon leads the premium athletic wear market.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Sara Appino – Updated Nov 20, 2026 at 4:05PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Colgate-Palmolive ›.

    Choosing between a steady staples giant and a premium apparel leader requires balancing reliability against growth potential. Investors must decide if Colgate-Palmolive (CL +1.89%) or lululemon athletica (LULU -2.76%) better suits their 2027 goals.

    According to recent reports, colgate-Palmolive dominates everyday essentials like toothpaste and pet nutrition, while Lululemon leads the premium athletic wear market. One offers defensive qualities in volatile markets, and the other aims for expansion in international retail. This comparison looks at their growth paths, financial health, and current valuations to help you navigate these two distinct paths.

    According to recent reports, colgate-Palmolive reaches consumers in more than 200 countries with a diverse portfolio including oral care, home hygiene, and specialty pet nutrition. In its latest annual report, Walmart (WMT +1.51%) and its affiliates accounted for nearly 11% of total net sales. Customer concentration like this adds a layer of risk, though the company continues to expand its presence in emerging markets among consumer staples stocks.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached approximately $21.3 billion, reflecting a growth rate of roughly 5.9%. Net income for the same period was close to $2.1 billion, resulting in a net margin of nearly 9.6%. These results indicate a consistent demand for hygiene and pet health products despite broader economic shifts.

    As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio reached approximately 158.4x, which represents the relationship between its total debt and shareholder equity. The current ratio, measuring the ability to pay short-term debts with current assets, was roughly 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was close to $3.6 billion.

    Lululemon Athletica operates a premium athletic lifestyle business focused on technical apparel, footwear, and accessories. The company uses an omni-channel approach, selling through over 800 stores and its own digital platforms. The company also uses license and supply arrangements with third parties to enter international markets like the UAE and Israel.

    In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached nearly $11.1 billion, representing a growth rate of approximately 1.7%. Net income for this period was roughly $1.4 billion, resulting in a net margin of nearly 12.8%. The slower revenue growth suggests a period of normalization following years of rapid post-pandemic expansion.

    As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was nearly 0.4x, showing the tech giant uses relatively little debt compared to its equity. The current ratio was approximately 2.3x, suggesting a strong ability to cover short-term obligations. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow reached close to $921.7 million.

    Colgate-Palmolive faces significant exposure to international markets and fluctuations in foreign currency values. The company deals with intense global competition from traditional rivals like Procter & Gamble (NYSE:PG) and newer private-label manufacturers. It also manages substantial legal uncertainty regarding ongoing talc-related litigation and operational risks from potential supply chain disruptions.

    Lululemon Athletica manages heightened competition in the athletic apparel market, especially from imitation products. The tech giant is vulnerable to supply chain disruptions because its manufacturing and fabric sourcing are concentrated in the APAC region. Additionally, it faces reputational risks from pending securities class action lawsuits and sensitivity to changes in U.S. tariff policy.

    Lululemon Athletica appears significantly cheaper than its peer, as it carries a lower Forward P/E and a lower P/S ratio, which measures sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    I'd go with Colgate-Palmolive. It sells everyday products around the world and has raised its dividend for 63 straight years, a record built on things people buy in any economy. It holds the biggest share of the world's toothpaste market, and its Hill's pet food brand adds a second source of growth.

    It has been revealed that last quarter, sales grew in nearly every region, emerging markets like India and Brazil led the way, and management raised its profit outlook. Costs are rising and U.S. shoppers are cautious, but those pressures are hitting the whole industry, and the rest of Colgate's business is still growing.

    Industry observers note that to be fair to lululemon, it has a premium brand and $1.4 billion in cash. But sales are shrinking, with North American shoppers buying less at existing stores, and the company cut its full-year outlook in its latest report. What's more, a fresh CEO is still reshaping the leadership team. For investors who want to buy and hold into 2027 and beyond, Colgate offers steady growth and a dividend that gets bigger every year.

    Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026, plus more AI workplace updates

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption.
    • During the keynote for the manufacturer’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.
    • Also: Microsoft states its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, AI-powered workspaces are tech companies’ latest focus, as the industry still struggles to perfect adoption. Microsoft has just put its offering into the ring.

    During the keynote for the manufacturer’s Ignite conference on Tuesday, CEO Satya Nadella announced Copilot Workspaces, a collaborative, “multiplayer” surface for Copilot’s agentic capabilities.

    Also: Microsoft states its upcoming AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost.

    The product, available in Frontier for now, is similar to OpenAI’s ChatGPT Space and several new Anthropic features, including Whiteboard and Sheets, which essentially merge the work tools you’re used to using with an agentic framework.

    Recent findings suggest that “As the evolution of Copilot Notebooks, it’s where people and agents build on each other’s work,” Microsoft stated. “An agent drafts a section of a document, and you review. You leave a comment, and an agent picks it up.”.

    Microsoft also confirmed Autopilot, a sort of counterpoint agent to Copilot that “can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work, and manage a project — without waiting for a prompt,” as Microsoft described.

    In a demo video during the keynote, the agent appeared to function similarly to OpenAI’s Dots, but for work — employees can tag their Autopilot “like a colleague,” Microsoft noted, and assign it tasks.

    Also: 4 ways Anthropic’s fresh Claude Sheets beat using a Google Sheets connector.

    Microsoft said the agent will be able to autonomously handle “meetings and follow-ups on its own,” though that claim may be best verified by teams themselves.

    Speaking of trust, however, Microsoft noted that “Autopilot runs on the identity, security, and compliance foundation IT already uses,” and that “each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager,” meaning IT can block it as needed.

    “Its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name, so security teams have a clear audit trail. Powered by Work IQ, it understands how your organization works within existing permissions,” Microsoft noted.

    The manufacturer added that employees will soon “be able to bring their personal Autopilot into Workspaces” as well. The feature is also available in Frontier.

    Sources indicate that nadella also announced a few other productivity features, including a “command center” called Today that spans email, calendar, meetings, tasks, and threads in Teams. Presently in private preview in Outlook and the Copilot app, it includes a personalized briefing and a feed of priorities that updates throughout the day.

    “The draft is written and ready for you to edit; the schedule change is already proposed; and the forgotten follow-up is waiting for you to send it, complete with context so you can catch up promptly,” Microsoft remarked of the feature, which sounds like an agentic briefing-cum-morning-assistant.

    Also: Nearly 70% of workers use AI regularly now – but many get no time to upskill.

    Recent findings suggest that microsoft also announced that Home, now generally available, unifies Chat and Cowork into a singular starting point. That’s similar to Anthropic’s recent consolidation of its chat and agentic Cowork offerings, demonstrating an overall trend toward simplification in workplace AI.

    While more companies are finally starting to see a return on their AI investment, agents are still expensive and can promptly rack up costs when unsupervised.

    Microsoft unveiled a few tools to track this at Ignite: Agent 365 Business Analytics and Agent 365 Cost Management.

    Also: Microsoft wants to put a dollar value on AI’s work – but can you trust the math?

    In a recent development, agent 365, which Microsoft announced last year, is the company’s observability platform. Microsoft remarked Business Analytics, in Frontier Public today, provides insights on what a company is spending on AI and why, and where it’s paying off, as well as forecasts future costs. In a demo during the keynote, Microsoft indicated how admins can see when specific agents’ costs have spiked recently and what (human) employee to notify as a result.

    “It starts with a new way to measure your investment: in work completed, not simply tokens,” Microsoft stated. “It analyzes the tasks, how long that work typically takes a person, and the share Cowork performed, providing a sophisticated view of the hours your intelligence supports and what the work is worth.”.

    Cost Management lets IT see where teams are using AI down to the model.

    “Leaders can set spending policies, limits, and proactive alerts and control which models are available,” Microsoft said. Anthropic released a similar tool last month, though it was focused more on making seats as efficient as possible on Teams and Enterprise intends.

    #27898. Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2218 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Everything Is Falling Apart, and AI’s Fingerprints Are All Over It

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2218 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.
    • It has been revealed that microsoft Outlook?
    • Something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I have struggled to find the time to write this story about why everything keeps breaking because everything keeps breaking.

    It has been revealed that microsoft Outlook? Broken, for a bit. Air traffic control? Had some complications. Bank with Chase? Monday was not great. But even before that, you had issues if you ran a website with PHP, or had a grocery store freezer connected to the internet, or owned crypto. I am almost certainly forgetting some.

    Something must be behind all of this, you might think—a massive cyberattack campaign, maybe or AI agents running amok across the internet? But the answer is more complicated than that. All of these problems, and the ones that will happen after I write this, are probably unconnected, at least in the concrete sense. But they exist in a world where the infrastructure of the internet and the whole human world it undergirds looks increasingly precarious.

    It has been revealed that adam Meyers, senior vice president of counter adversary operations at cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike, called last month “Black October.” This month? “Blacker November.” December probably isn’t looking great.

    “This is not getting better, unfortunately,” Meyers told me.

    One big reason for all of this, although not the only one, is artificial intelligence, but maybe not in the ways you expect.

    Recent findings suggest that if it’s connected to the internet, it’s at risk. Websites, sure. But also utilities like power plants and water treatment facilities or, for some reason, grocery store freezers.

    In the olden days, like six months ago, a hacker taking control would have required a fairly complicated set of skills, honed over a long career, perhaps in the employ of a government or criminal organization.

    Sources indicate that artificial intelligence, especially models developed and released this year, has changed things. AI has “democratized” hacking, cybersecurity experts told me. Things that used to require the capabilities and focus of a team of people with a clear goal can be done by a 20-something with an AI model and a specially designed program around it. And you don’t have to be a big or valuable target anymore to be worthy of a hacker’s attention.

    Sources indicate that at the same time, AI has made it easier to find vulnerabilities. These models and agents — essentially AI models that can do things on their own — can comb through websites or code and find problems that might have escaped the notice of humans. And they can do so more cheaply, meaning they can be turned on code that might not otherwise have gotten a close look. So many vulnerabilities are being exposed that it’s been given an appropriately bleak name: the vulnpocalypse.

    Even that defensive advantage is a double-edged sword. Before, it might have taken weeks before a newly discovered vulnerability could be exploited. Now it might take days, even hours. If you’re responsible for a website or any of those things connected to the internet that may or may not still be maintained by their creators, you may not be paying attention and know you should enhancement. You may find yourself liable if a breach leads to a leak of customer data. You may not have the know-how to fix it.

    It has been revealed that another risk introduced by AI is that the technology, trained on all the lines of code its creators could find, is really good at writing code. Software engineers know this, and companies are now maintaining smaller teams of human engineers using AI to write more and more software. That code might be OK, but it might not be, and there’s a chance no human ever looked at it to be sure.

    Sources indicate that when I connected with John Strand over video chat, he was in Germany for a conference, and he was smiling. That wasn’t good. “You need to understand that whenever an offensive security person smiles and gets excited,” he noted, “it’s bad.”.

    As owner and CEO of Black Hills Information Security, Strand’s job is to test systems for weaknesses, to think like an attacker and poke holes in a client’s defenses. He claims he’d been getting a bit bored with the work after decades of the same techniques until the cyber capabilities of AI models started to explode at the end of 2025. New AI models were great at finding weaknesses in code, and AI agents could do the boring, time-consuming part.

    “You’re seeing something that can automate the kind of grinding grunt work of offensive security and bring that to a human operator much faster,” Strand remarked.

    Things have only accelerated since the summer. AI agents are capable of more autonomy. And attackers have better tools to refine the often blunt instruments of AI models — harnesses. While an AI model can do a lot of things, a harness provides the tools and direction that allow it to do a specific thing more effectively. Think Anthropic’s Claude Code or OpenAI’s Codex, but for hacking. Perhaps the biggest, most notable harness used by hackers is Artex, a significant-enough threat that the FBI issued a warning last week.

    In September and October, a hack of major South Korean banks led to the theft of personal information. Meyers states CrowdStrike determined the attacker was likely a 26-year-old in China using Artex. After asking AI how to do the attack, the hacker succeeded, then asked the AI how to sell the stolen data on Telegram.

    “Anybody out there can now be a nation-state-level hacker just by using the tool,” Meyers said.

    Despite efforts by major AI developers to limit who can access their biggest and most capable models, the hacking and exploit skills attackers need are within the means of models already in the hands of attackers. That includes open-weight models that hackers can run on their own hardware, away from the guardrails and peering eyes of AI companies and government agencies.

    “The genie’s out of the bottle, and there’s no putting it back in,” said Gary Barlet, public sector chief technology officer at Illumio, a firm that specializes in ransomware and breach containment.

    AI-powered hackers, whether they’re individual vibe-hackers or government-backed cyberwarfare units intent on damaging critical infrastructure, always have an advantage. They just have to be right once, as the saying goes. Defenders have to be right every time.

    Sources indicate that the good thing is that the defenders are using the same tools as the attackers. And sometimes they have a head start. Programs like Anthropic’s Project Glasswing, OpenAI’s Daybreak and Google’s Fairwind let cybersecurity experts and high-profile targets like banks and healthcare providers have early access to the most capable models from those developers, often with fewer limits on what the models can find. The goal is to get a jump on patching and fixing the easiest and riskiest problems.

    Industry observers note that it still might not be enough, and Significant Tech leaders know it. In an October appearance at the Stanford Graduate School of Business, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said he no longer thought we’d be able to “just patch all the bugs” and that the problem is one that “is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders or countries or individuals, taken seriously.”.

    According to recent reports, and defenders may not have much of a lead in patching bugs anyway, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella mentioned this week at the Fresh York Times Dealbook Summit. Previously, when patching a critical system, you might have a week to test it before pushing it to production. “Right now the patch needs to go instantly from being available to being patched in production because it’s being exploited in the wild,” Nadella said. “That’s going to create instability.”.

    The PHP vulnerability widely reported in October — with an urgent notice from the PHP Foundation for website owners to patch — stemmed from work through Patch the Planet, part of OpenAI’s Daybreak.

    That’s just one high-profile recent disclosure. But there has been an avalanche of them. The National Vulnerability Database has received more than 10,000 instances of common vulnerabilities and exposures so far in November, after more than 17,000 CVEs in October. For comparison, in October 2025, that figure was less than 5,000.

    “There’s effectively this substantial backlog of security issues in the open-source world that hadn’t been discovered until AI was able to just spend tons of time analyzing it and finding these vulnerabilities,” noted Matt Wyckhouse, CEO of Finite State, a cybersecurity manufacturer focused on connected devices.

    Industry observers note that it goes well beyond open-source software. The connected devices Wyckhouse focuses on include things like refrigerators and smart home gadgets — the kinds of things that probably didn’t have to be connected to the internet, but are. The source code of the firmware and software powering those products has been seen by far fewer eyes than something like PHP, an incredibly common coding language used by much of the internet. The code running these devices may not be on GitHub or floating around the internet, but an AI model might be able to reverse-engineer it and find an exploit. And suddenly an attacker can turn freezers into ovens. If you think ground beef is expensive now, imagine what would happen if a major retailer’s stock of hamburger all spoiled overnight.

    “Refrigeration has to work for our society to function, as it turns out,” Wyckhouse mentioned.

    Wherever the vulnerability is found, it has to be patched. That’s where the backlog of problems is really wreaking havoc. Companies that create or just operate software are swamped with notable, critical issues that have to be fixed now because it could only be hours before an attacker can exploit it. It’s why your computer and the software on it have to update so frequently these days.

    “It’s daunting the amount of work and the amount of time it’s going to take to clean this whole thing up,” said Ted Miracco, CEO of the mobile security firm Approov.

    And patching isn’t perfect. Sometimes it’s not a cyberattack that causes a system to go down but the fix to prevent it. Software updates are believed to be responsible for several of the recent high-profile outages, including Apple’s concerns on Tuesday.

    Things get even hairier if the code isn’t great to begin with or presents latest problems of its own. And with AI writing even more of it, that’s a growing concern.

    In the backdrop of all of this chaos is the fact that software engineering is one of the industries most disrupted by AI. Models trained on miles of code are great at writing something that works — no matter how many holes are in it. And to CEOs eager to cut costs and boost their companies’ stock prices, the temptation is to lay off engineers and have fewer people use AI to do all that coding.

    It has been revealed that substantial Tech has been laying off staff by the thousands this year. Microsoft’s October announcement that it was offering buyouts to 60,000 staff became a key talking point just weeks later when the system powering its Outlook email service went dark for a day. Might things break less often if more people were on hand to maintain them?

    “I wouldn’t be surprised if companies start to backtrack on that more,” stated Ryan McCurdy, vice president of marketing at the database security firm Liquibase.

    Companies might also have more junior developers writing and releasing code that would have previously gone through senior developers, with AI replacing the productivity, but not the experience, McCurdy says.

    That means the problem isn’t just the vulnerabilities in existing software, but the vulnerabilities being written into latest software or patches to existing software by AI. The same technology is causing the problem, providing the solution and complicating that solution.

    According to recent reports, the main thing we can do now is just… wait. Wyckhouse told me he thinks the next two years are going to be a period of growing pains as vulnerabilities are found and patched. The end result should be that everything is more stable.

    According to recent reports, “I think software is going to be an order of magnitude more secure by the end of the next year or two than it is today for this reason,” he mentioned. “It will hurt a bit.”.

    Whether you’re an ordinary phone user or a major corporation, updating your software has become more key than ever.

    According to recent reports, “You’ve got to patch. You go for a flu shot, and you go and have your preventative healthcare,” Meyers said. “You need to do the same thing when it comes to cybersecurity.”.

    It has been revealed that but consumers aren’t without power, especially when it comes to data breaches. If a company isn’t properly maintaining its systems and protecting your privacy or security online, don’t use it. Having your data hacked and compromised has become ordinary. We get letters in the mail saying someone stole data from our bank or doctor’s office, and if we jump through the following hoops, we can get 12 months of identity protection.

    We don’t have to put up with it, Barlet says. “I think we need to start having higher expectations from the companies we’re consuming from,” he noted.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant.
    • Also: Microsoft notes its newly introduced AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.
    • Recent findings suggest that MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    During the keynote at its Ignite conference on Tuesday, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella announced several new models from Microsoft AI (MAI), its lab within the tech giant. But new model releases are almost a dime a dozen these days, and accelerating fast — what really stood out was how Microsoft will let its customers access those models.

    Also: Microsoft notes its newly introduced AI coding model rivals Claude Opus 5.5.

    Recent findings suggest that MAI mentioned it would allow its customers to customize its frontier models with their own data and run them securely in Azure through an initiative called Licensed Weights. It’s essentially a selective approach to open-weight AI: more so than proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, but not fully downloadable on Hugging Face like Mistral’s Le Chonk. Interested companies will need to go through their Microsoft account reps to get started.

    “You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay entirely yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents,” Mustafa Suleyman, CEO of MAI, mentioned during the keynote.

    The approach should stand out to businesses looking for affordable AI that lets them retain control over their IP. Microsoft remarked it would only use customers’ information to train its models if they agreed.

    “No one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model,” Suleyman said during the keynote, a nod to an argument Palantir CEO Alex Karp has made repeatedly.

    According to recent reports, the dominant, if simplified, narrative in AI has been that proprietary, expensive models boast peak capabilities but aren’t customizable, while open, cheaper models are customizable but less capable. Microsoft’s AI models don’t necessarily compete with OpenAI and Anthropic yet, but the tech giant has legacy sway with countless businesses. By offering a customizable AI option, it could strike a balance among major tech companies.

    In a recent development, western labs, including Thinking Machines and Mistral, are releasing more competitive open-weight models, but Anthropic and OpenAI still have the overwhelming majority of the enterprise AI market. Though Licensed Weights isn’t an open-weight family of models, it does diversify the open-versus-closed debate a bit and differentiate Microsoft’s offering from OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s. It’s also a smart pairing with Microsoft’s goal to balance price and performance, if businesses find it impressive enough.

    Also: Microsoft unveiled Copilot Workspaces at Ignite 2026.

    “Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot, MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and against Opus 5.5 it’s an incredible 5% of that cost,” Suleyman noted of the upcoming coding model the tech giant announced at Ignite.

    It has been revealed that the company also released its new image editing model, MAI Image 2.7, on Tuesday, which now leads the category on Artificial Analysis while beating Nano Banana Pro and several GPT image models on price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft has positioned itself for organizations seeking a reliable blend of ROI tools, customization, security controls, and capability.
