    #27894. One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1104 w)
    📖 Baca
    Gadgets ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    One Month and a Half-Million-Plus Folds Later, Our Machine Is Still Testing the iPhone Duo

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1104 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago.
    • How many times can we fold the iPhone Duo?
    • It has been revealed that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, apple’s $1,999 iPhone Duo folding phone came out a month ago. Every day since then, 24 hours a day, seven days a week, a dedicated machine inside CNET’s lab has been folding and unfolding it over and over again. For science.

    How many times can we fold the iPhone Duo? As of Friday, Nov. 20, we’re up to more than 565,000 folds and the Duo hasn’t broken yet. The hinge has shown signs of potential failure, however. Our technicians, as well as the cameras and sensors that are part of our testing rig, continue to monitor the situation and collect data.

    It has been revealed that I oversee hardware and software testing as director of lab operations in our lab in Louisville, Kentucky. My team and I designed and built this proprietary machine to test foldable phones like Apple’s and its Samsung rival, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 (which we’ve also started testing). I’ve worked on the methodology and build of this testing rig for months in anticipation of Apple’s long-rumored foldable iPhone.

    We even named our machine to match its purpose: Meet the Fold-a-Phone.

    My team of engineers and testing experts has been watching the iPhone Duo open and close, over and over, for the past few weeks to rigorously and systematically monitor the durability of Apple’s hinge and two screens.

    After all, repeatedly folding a phone with bare hands can only get you so far in understanding the complex forces at play between the magnetics that snap the screen shut and the all-critical hinge.

    CNET’s Senior Technology Reporter, Abrar Al-Heeti, has done a beautiful job capturing the iPhone Duo’s pros and cons in her smart, thorough review as well as her one-month-later follow-up. Our Fold-a-Phone machine will add a deep data foundation to complement her real-world experience.

    Since Apple hasn’t publicly shared claims of the iPhone Duo’s foldable lifespan, CNET’s Fold-a-Phone machine is poised to provide a wealth of valuable data about Apple’s first foldable phone and competing models in the foldable market.

    And yes, you’d better believe we will use our treasure trove of in-house data to share status updates and comparisons during our ongoing testing window with the Duo.

    Sources indicate that join CNET’s iPhone Duo livestream on YouTube weekdays from 1 p.m. to 5 p.m. ET, where you can follow along live and watch the Fold-a-Phone do its thing to a Duo.

    Recent findings suggest that the importance of this moment is hard to overstate. Apple’s appearance on the foldable smartfold frontier lags Samsung by seven years (the first Galaxy Fold went on sale in the US in September 2019). Motorola and other phone-makers have long experimented with foldable phones in every shape and size, including a trifold accordion foldable phone we first demoed in 2019.

    CNET’s mobile experts, including Al-Heeti and Editor at Large Andrew Lanxon, have discussed the legitimizing effect of the iPhone Duo’s existence on the entire foldable phone landscape, which has previously felt like a new-wave fantasy rather than a mainstream riptide.

    In many ways, Apple’s newfound competition with existing foldable phones completes the portfolio. That is precisely why we’re building the Fold-a-Phone now, and why our proprietary machine, methodology and test data will enrich our collective understanding of the capabilities – and yes, limitations – of foldable phones as our true next-generation mobile device.

    Most current foldable phones are rated for 200,000 to 500,000 folds. As such, we knew we needed to create a robust and adaptable machine that could accommodate book- and flip-style foldable phones of any size, dimension and hinge orientation. (Note: The Fold-a-Phone was not built for trifold phones, which present a unique element to the engineering challenge.).

    Moreover, we wanted to test the phone the way people would actually use it. No one just sits around opening and closing their foldable phone at top speed all day. Rather, you open it naturally, spend a few minutes watching a video, browsing a web page, or using an app, close it, and then put it in your pocket. This may happen dozens of times per day.

    Mimicking this usage on the Fold-a-Phone limits undue stress on the phone hinge and avoids generating excess heat compared to a test built for speed.

    We determined that a cadence of roughly 4 seconds could sidestep technical hurdles while also being reasonably fast. The foldable phone takes 1 second to open, 1 second to fully open, 1 second to close and 1 second to fully close. This cycle counts as a single completed fold. Then, the cycle repeats until either the hinge or the screen gives out.

    Industry observers note that in conceptualizing and building the Fold-a-Phone, our team has used standard, off-the-shelf components to simplify the machine’s development. The essential design consists of two armatures, distinctly designed to perform the opening and closing movements with both force and grace.

    In a recent development, an industrial-grade stepper motor drives each armature, with the host software (running on a connected computer) deterministically adjusting the torque to complete each step of the process while also protecting the phone. If any of the several proximity sensors fail to detect the armature in the correct position, the machine stops immediately.

    Recent findings suggest that we also monitor the motors’ power usage to track how well the foldable phone opens and closes over time. We have set up cameras to capture images and video of the test from multiple angles, and we will analyze regular status updates from the computer to determine the current status of the phone and the test.

    To ensure we never miss a major development, the entire rig is connected to an EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus power station to guard against electricity outages, and all the output data is saved to multiple locations.

    To secure each phone to the machine, we use our CNET Lab Test-winning 3D printer, the Prusa Core One, to 3D-print a custom “sled” that matches each phone’s exact dimensions. We secure the phone to the sled with heavy-duty double-sided tape (yes, it works!) and then screw the sled onto the machine.

    Sources indicate that there’s always room for improvement. We’re constantly looking for ways to make the machine run more smoothly and quietly without disrupting the folding rhythm.

    Apple’s presence is already changing the game and could very well spur innovation in ways we can’t predict today. But until then, our Fold-a-Phone machine will continue to test the iPhone Duo and its competitors, and CNET’s writers will report on how well these individual hinged devices stand up to the challenge – or fold under pressure.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ubuntu 27.04, Tenacious T-Rex, is set for an April 22, 2027 release. Although that seems a long way off, it’s sooner than you think. As is implied by the release number, 27.04 is not an LTS release, so it only receives support for nine months (until January 2028). The good news is that you can migrate from 27.04 to 27.10, and then to the LTS release, 28.04. The entire upgrade path ensures that you don’t have to miss a single release.

    But what’s coming in Ubuntu 27.04? Given that it’s an interim release, you’re probably assuming that there’ll be nothing exciting to be found. Although there won’t be any game-changing additions, there will be plenty of refinements and bug fixes.

    Also: I’ve used Ubuntu for 22 years – and 26.10 might be its best release yet.

    Recent findings suggest that I’ve been using the daily release of Ubuntu 27.04 for a bit. Let’s take a look at what is currently expected in Tenacious T-Rex.

    This is probably the biggest addition to the next release of Ubuntu. And although you won’t find any major changes in GNOME, there are some important ones. First off, there will be editable quick settings, which allow for customizing, adding, removing, and rearranging toggles and widgets. GNOME 52 will also enjoy a revamped calendar popover, which streamlines the feature to focus primarily on events, time, and weather.

    Also: Over Ubuntu? Fedora is the Linux distro I’d hop to next – here’s why.

    There will also be several improvements to window management, such as a spatial overview and a mosaic/tiling system for auto-resizing and organizing windows, a refined full-screen Alt+Tab app switcher, which will be capable of grouping older windows by application while showing newer ones individually, and finally, the ability to remember window sizing, placement, and workspace.

    Desktop search is also getting a bit of polish by way of a redesigned popover and an improved results overlay that includes file previews, multiple actions, and search filters. And, as usual, there will be plenty of bug fixes and performance enhancements. The bump in speed is noticeable, too, in my testing.

    Ubuntu 27.04 will ship with the Linux 7.6 kernel, which includes better VRAM management for gaming and expanded support for modern hardware, such as early enablement for AMD Zen 6, stable support for Intel Xe3P, mainline boot capabilities for Apple M3 Pro/Max/Ultra, and initial support for the 2026 Steam Controller.

    There will also be performance gains for both the Btrfs and Ext4 file systems, which (along with the improvements in GNOME 52) will make Ubuntu 27.04 one of the best-performing releases in some time.

    Also: This lightweight Linux distro revives old PCs destined for the junk pile – and it’s beautiful.

    Industry observers note that one thing that surprised me is that Myna (Ubuntu’s AI dictation tool) has yet to find its way into the Ubuntu ISO as a default app. As with Ubuntu 26.10, you can install it, but you have to first add the necessary repository with:.

    With the repository added, you can install it with:.

    Once installed, you can use it as expected.

    As of right now, that’s all we know about Tenacious T-Rex.

    It’s so early in the release cycle that it still uses the default 26.10 wallpaper, but there will be more information soon. I will say this: I’ve come to count on Ubuntu’s latest releases to be an improvement over the previous iterations, and from what I’ve seen so far in my testing, 27.04 will not disappoint. It may not knock you back to prehistoric times, but Tenacious T-Rex will wow you with its performance and polished looks.

    Also: Linux has hundreds of distros: 5 reasons to stop using the same few.

    Google Gemini Partners With Watch Duty to Clear Static From Firefighter Radio

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that on Friday, Google’s Gemini team declared the results of a new partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders.
    • According to recent reports, the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert.
    • In a recent development, “This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” noted Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that on Friday, Google’s Gemini team declared the results of a new partnership with the wildfire-tracking app Watch Duty, after Gemini engineers spent six months embedded with Watch Duty’s first responders. The results cut vital new wildfire dispatch translations down to seconds and helped improve radio communications, which can be rough on the front lines of a new fire.

    According to recent reports, the Gemini AI improvements got a real-world test during Washington state’s Railroad Fire in July 2026, when Watch Duty issued what it calls its first-ever nighttime Critical Alert. The alert stemmed from a nearly unintelligible, static-filled 911 call that the Gemini tool transcribed in under 30 seconds. That kind of assistance can help Watch Duty send alerts to affected communities more rapidly and enable first responders to enhancement maps more accurately and make better-informed decisions.

    In a recent development, “This is something the tool also has the capability to do if reports of flooding are communicated via radio,” noted Dave Merritt, co-founder and chief technology officer of Watch Duty. “Across disasters, we hear feedback every day that first responders are using Watch Duty for additional situational awareness, especially for disasters that span multiple counties.”.

    Watch Duty reporters are active and retired first responders who can manually monitor up to 20 different feeds, though static and rapid-fire jargon can make them difficult to follow.

    Gemini workers used more than 20,000 hours of Watch Duty radio recordings to train the AI tool to recognize firefighting terms that aren’t in the average dictionary or books that AIs are typically trained on.

    Google says the tool is not designed to replace human decision-making in life-or-death situations.

    “This tool takes on the demanding work of listening, freeing Watch Duty’s volunteers to focus on what matters most: confirming fires and getting warnings to people while they can still act,” said Stephanie Chew, Google project team lead.

    The project was completed at no cost thanks to a Google.org fellowship, and the resulting Watch Duty app features are free to use.

    From the data collected, Gemini engineers and Watch Duty identified several measures of success.

    One metric was the word error rate, which fell by around 15% after the AI model was implemented. Another sign of success was a jump in Watch Duty volunteers’ satisfaction with their radio transcription tools, from around 35% to 92%.

    In a recent development, the Gemini tool continues to analyze approximately 200 hours of radio speech traffic from 400 feeds per day. The tool was made to handle more than 10,000 radio feeds if necessary.

    In a recent development, the integration could pave the way for broader use across public safety. The platform’s built-in scalability could eventually bring similar audio-clearing tools to local fire departments, 911 call centers and Coast Guard operations, where clear communication is critical under pressure.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6.

    • But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, look, we weren’t all lucky enough to lock in PTO for the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Not everyone gets to write a review of the most anticipated video game in recent memory, or live blog their first 24 hours roaming around Vice City.

    A lot of folks are still working away, daydreaming about getting back on the sticks and knocking off corner stores as Jason and Lucia right now. Some people are even on work trips or vacations away from their home consoles right now – let’s keep them in our thoughts.

    But even if you find yourself away from home, that doesn’t mean you’re completely locked out of playing GTA 6. Sure, the game may at the moment be console-locked to the PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, but there are still clever ways to get the game booted up when you’re on the go.

    Here’s everything you need to know about the remote play features that you’ll need to take this modern Bonnie and Clyde story on the road.

    So long as you have a PS5 or an Xbox with GTA 6 downloaded and ready to go, you can experience the game through smaller devices even when you’re away from home.

    Both modern consoles support remote play, a feature that lets you stream your game from your home setup.

    Sources indicate that if you’re looking to turn on the Xbox’s remote play feature, you need to access the Profile & System settings in the Xbox guide. From there, you need to navigate to the Devices & Connections menu and choose the Remote features option.

    In a recent development, you’ll need to enable the remote features and put your console into sleep mode in order to pair your chosen remote play device. Remote play devices include smartphones, tablets and Windows computers.

    Gamers who own a PlayStation 5 will need to follow similar steps to get remote play functioning on a mobile device. Within the PlayStation’s settings menu, navigate to the System tab and choose Remote Play. Toggle the Enable Remote Play option. From there, all of the necessary device pairing and gameplay setup will happen through the PS Remote Play app, which you can download on your handheld device.

    Whether you own a PlayStation or an Xbox, you’ll want to ensure your console settings are tuned so it stays connected to the internet in rest mode. You’ll also need to enable the console to turn on via a network connection. These settings will allow you to start a remote play session anytime, even if you’ve already left your home.

    According to recent reports, if you’re using PlayStation’s remote play feature, you don’t have to fiddle around with gaming tablets or third-party handheld devices in order to find a comfortable way to play GTA 6. Sony’s PlayStation Portal is the perfect console accessory for natural gameplay, since it retains the DualShock controller design.

    GTA 6 isn’t coming out on PC for a while still. That limits how many options you have when it comes to taking the game on the go with you. If (for whatever reason) you don’t have access to any remote play options, that leaves you with only the most inconvenient and unwieldy way to take the new crime simulator with you on the road.

    You’ll have to lug around your PS5 or Xbox wherever you go to get in some GTA time – but hey, at least the gaming industry’s deteriorating respect for physical media means you won’t have to keep track of a disc.

    In a recent development, the PS5 Slim is probably the easiest current-gen console to carry with you, since the digital edition weighs less than 6 pounds. But you’re giving up the best possible performance available on the PS5 Pro.

    Either way, you’ll be carrying around a large, expensive piece of hardware, so this option should only be considered if you really can’t get remote play functioning for whatever reason.

    Industry observers note that microsoft’s video game ecosystem is huge, with Game Pass and streaming options available for PC players. But the Xbox brand isn’t offering gamers a cheat code to play GTA 6 on their beefy rigs (or any convenient handheld devices).

    Sources indicate that GTA 6 is only available on Xbox consoles with Xbox Cloud Gaming at this time. The upside is that this option lets you play the boundary-pushing new game on the Xbox One, which is very close to being two console generations old.

    At that point, you’re better off biting the bullet on a current-generation console and considering the available remote play options.

    Twenty percent of holiday shoppers are using AI agents as their first stop for research and advice, but they are not ready to have agents make purchases, according to the latest Salesforce research.

    Also: What to know about early Black Friday sales.

    Recent findings suggest that salesforce surveyed more than 2,500 shoppers in the US, UK, Canada, and Australia and found that 74% of shoppers trust recommendations from AI agents. Salesforce research forecasts AI-driven shopping recommendations to drive $75.8 billion in Cyber Week spending, up 13% from 2025.

    Industry observers note that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

    Brands are also being noticed by AI agents, with 30% of shoppers saying they were first introduced to a new brand via AI. And most importantly, 1 in 10 (11%) shoppers would avoid a brand if an AI agent told them to.

    Here are some of the key findings from the 2026 holiday shopping research.

    It has been revealed that retailers that use AI shopping agents are seeing bigger orders and more loyal customers. The survey found that shoppers who use AI agent referrals are twice as likely to make a purchase. In addition, 39% of shoppers have used AI agents on an e-commerce site, and 80% had a positive experience, while 75% felt more loyal to the brand as a result of the AI agent experience.

    Shoppers who use AI agents spend 8% more than the average buyer and purchase 23% more items per order. Brands that use AI agents are seeing seven times faster sales growth than brands without them.

    It has been revealed that 1 in 3 consumers has used an AI agent, including the widely adopted Meta Muse, now used by 12% of all consumers. Grok Bot is also in high demand.

    Sources indicate that the survey found that 28% of consumers give their agents multiple tasks per day. The most common use of AI agents is price comparisons, product reviews, and brainstorming for gift items. Brand discovery is a major benefit of AI agent use cases.

    Agents as advisors are growing, but agents are not buying products yet, with only 19% of personal agent users using logic to check out. Only 9% of consumers allow their personal AI agents to have unrestricted access to their financial details, and 36% have set up a separate credit card for their AI agents.

    Also: ZDNET’s favorite tech devices for 2026.

    The majority of consumers (73%) are not comfortable giving personal AI agents their payment information, and 49% are not interested in agents making purchases on their behalf. Consumers do not want to share their purchase history or personal data that could potentially lead to unwanted charges. Shoppers will abandon an AI agent after 2-3 mistakes. If an AI agent makes a bad recommendation, 1 in 3 consumers will blame the AI.

    Retailers must adopt AI shopping agents in order to compete. Retailers must be able to service and respond to shopper agents. The ability to detect intent, buying signals, sources of dissatisfaction, and other consumer-related buying patterns at machine scale (significantly faster and higher volume than human scale) will require retailers to invest in AI agentic engagement capabilities.

    Also: 50 AI agents tried to build a thriving Minecraft civilization – it didn’t end well.

    Today, AI agents advise consumers on their holiday shopping journeys, but in the very near future, they will autonomously make purchasing decisions with little to no involvement from their human counterparts. The future of shopping will be more autonomous, highly personalized, and nearly frictionless. Brands that invest in agentic AI will garner the most loyalty and future business.

    iOS 27.3 Could Bring the Redesigned Health App and a More Capable Siri AI to Your Device Soon

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1042 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Apple released the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov.
    • Apple historically releases an iOS upgrade in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.
    • Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Apple released the second public beta of iOS 27.3 on Thursday, Nov. 19, more than two months after the launch of the iPhone 18 Pro lineup and iOS 27. The headliner here is the return of the new Health app: After briefly testing the redesigned Health app in an early iOS 27.2 beta, Apple has put the revamped app back in the recent beta cycle.

    Apple historically releases an iOS upgrade in December, so I expect iOS 27.3 to land on iPhones later this year.

    Since this is a beta, I recommend downloading it on something other than your primary device. This isn’t the final version of iOS 27.3, so the update might be buggy and battery life may be short, so it’s best to keep those troubles on a secondary device.

    Also, since this isn’t the final version, there could be more features to land on your iPhone when Apple releases 27.3.

    Here are some features developers and beta testers can try now in the second iOS 27.3 beta.

    The redesigned Health app returns in the iOS 27.3 beta after Apple tested the feature in the iOS 27.2 beta process. Developers and beta testers can explore the refreshed app and see things like a latest Longevity tab and your Health Age.

    Apple wrote online that we can expect the redesigned Health app to land on devices later this year.

    If developers and beta testers have an Apple Watch that is running the watchOS 27.3 beta as well as an iPhone running the iOS 27.3 beta, those folks can test out Apple’s Live Rewind and Siri Recap in Audio Intelligence.

    Live Rewind allows you to pull up a text transcript of a conversation in the past 15 seconds on your Apple Watch, and Siri Recap can automatically give you a summary of meetings, conversations and other events. Live Rewind snippets are replaced by new audio and then deleted, and Siri Recaps delete themselves after seven days if you don’t manually delete them sooner. However, you can also save both of these in the Siri app and export them to the Notes or Journal apps on your iPhone.

    While both Live Rewind and Siri Recap are automatically deleted over time, I’m uncomfortable with the ability to save snippets or recaps, which raises concerns about people recording my conversations without my knowledge. Even if Audio Intelligence just summarizes what I said, I still find both features creepy.

    And while I recognize the utility for certain groups of people, I also think it’s better to just, y’know… talk to someone instead of asking your watch what they just mentioned.

    According to recent reports, siri AI gets a huge enhancement in the iOS 27.3 beta. The feature can now do more actions in supported apps, like Apple Music and Messages. For example, if you go into Apple Music, you can ask Siri to create a playlist for you, and in Messages, you can ask Siri to schedule, edit or unsend messages. If you open an app and ask Siri what it can do, the digital assistant should give you some examples of its capabilities.

    You can also use Siri in Safari to scan an entire webpage — even parts of the page that aren’t in your direct view — to give you helpful information. So if you are looking at a menu online, you can ask Siri to find the gluten-free or vegetarian options.

    The beta also brings Siri AI to traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish and Norwegian.

    According to recent reports, in the latest iOS 27.3 beta, developers and beta testers can find video podcasts in the Apple TV app, as well as in the Podcasts app. You can find video podcasts by going into the app, tapping Home across the bottom of your screen and scrolling down to the Video Podcasts section.

    This means you can watch a video podcast in the Apple TV app on your iPhone while commuting, and then you can finish that video later on an Apple TV 4K or another device with access to Apple TV.

    Each workout recommends exercises, reps, sets and weights in order to help you meet your goals. And if you’re unfamiliar with an exercise, you can also watch video tutorials to see how to perform that exercise.

    In a recent development, standBy mode also gets an upgrade in the iOS 27.3 beta. In the beta, you can add full weather and calendar slides to the mode and choose from more colors.

    It has been revealed that apple introduced StandBy mode alongside iOS 17, and it was one of my favorite iPhone features. I’m happy Apple is finally showing it some love and adding more features and capabilities so it feels more like a home or desk hub.

    If you’re a fan of dark mode, the iOS 27.3 beta has a treat for you. The beta gives you a new setting in Safari called Adaptive Dark Mode. When enabled, it forces dark mode onto webpages in Safari that may not have a dark mode option otherwise.

    Here’s where to find the option.

    1. Tap Settings.2. Tap Apps.3. Tap Safari.4. Tap Adaptive Dark Mode.5. Tap On.

    If you have an iPhone Duo and are running the iOS 27.3 beta, you have fresh options to lock and unlock your device. In the beta, you can enable your device to lock simply by closing the Duo. You can find this option in Settings and within the Display & Brightness menu.

    Next, people with the Duo can unlock the device using that phone’s front camera and without opening the foldable. You will have had to recently unlocked your device with Touch ID or your passcode. You can find this option in Settings and in the Touch ID & Passcode menu.

    Industry observers note that those are a few of the fresh features developers can try now with the second beta of iOS 27.3. Apple has not mentioned when exactly it will release iOS 27.3 to the general public, but we expect it to land on devices before the end of the year.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting.
    • Recent findings suggest that zoom out and the damage is even bigger.
    • Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jonathan Ponciano – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:07PM EST.

    Nvidia's terrible month just got worse.

    Sources indicate that shares of Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) fell 14% on Friday afternoon, to less than $126, after Reuters reported that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the chipmaker's accounting. The drop erased roughly $491 billion in market value in a single session, taking Nvidia from about $3.52 trillion to about $3.03 trillion.

    Recent findings suggest that zoom out and the damage is even bigger. Nvidia closed at a record $239.24 on Oct. 6. At Friday's price, the stock is down about 48% from that high, and the firm has lost about $2.7 trillion in value in just six weeks.

    Here's what we know, and what investors should make of it.

    The Wall Street Journal first reported on Tuesday that the SEC was investigating Nvidia but couldn't say what the probe was about. On Friday, Reuters, citing two people briefed on the matter, reported that the agency's enforcement staff are examining potential accounting issues at the company.

    Recent findings suggest that many questions remain unanswered. Reuters couldn't determine when the inquiry began or which accounting practices are under review. The SEC declined to comment, and Nvidia didn't immediately respond. Keep in mind that the SEC investigates plenty of companies that are never charged with anything.

    The stock was already having a bad day before the report: shares were down more than 6% earlier in the session amid a broad sell-off in AI stocks.

    The probe adds to a pile of problems. Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov. 11 following revelations about his personal relationships, including with a woman U.S. authorities suspect of spying for China, which China denies. The Justice Department is also reviewing Nvidia's planned $12.9 billion purchase of Hugging Face, according to Reuters.

    It has been revealed that two areas could draw scrutiny. The first is how Nvidia reports where its sales come from. The tech giant breaks out revenue by where customers are headquartered, rather than where they're billed. On that basis, about 63% of last quarter's revenue came from U.S.-based customers. The Financial Times has reported that Nvidia made the switch as sales billed to Singapore approached half of its total, a bad look with Southeast Asia having become a hub for chips smuggled into China.

    It has been revealed that the second is how Nvidia helps its customers pay for its chips. On Tuesday's earnings call, interim CEO Colette Kress noted Nvidia's guarantees totaled $118 billion at the end of the quarter, including $105 billion of credit support tied to a single data center campus. These guarantees are the kind of disclosure the SEC is watching closely at AI companies. When a chipmaker helps fund the projects that buy its chips, it's harder to tell how much demand would exist on its own.

    It has been revealed that none of this has shown up in the numbers yet. Nvidia's revenue jumped 103% to $115.8 billion last quarter, and the organization expects about $130 billion this quarter. Management even raised its growth forecast for next fiscal year to about 75%. At about $126, the stock trades at roughly 12 times last quarter's adjusted earnings of $2.68 per share on an annualized basis, cheap for a company growing this fast.

    Recent findings suggest that but cheap can get cheaper. Accounting questions hit at the heart of what investors pay for: trust in the numbers. Until Nvidia names a permanent CEO and the SEC's focus becomes clearer, the stock could stay volatile, even after a 48% drop.

    Sources indicate that for long-term investors who already own Nvidia, there's no need to panic-sell on a report about an investigation. For anyone thinking of buying, it's smarter to wait for more clarity, or to build a position slowly, than to bet that the worst is over. There are plenty of other semiconductor stocks without a cloud of investigations hanging over them.

    • Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting.
    • According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent?

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Just months after its release, Google is making its Spark agent free and officially renaming its capabilities “Tasks.” You can now toggle to it from the standard Gemini Chat setting. Reports show the rebrand started gradually in mid-October.

    According to recent reports, also: Ready for a Siri AI agent? Apple under pressure to upgrade its assistant faster.

    Sources indicate that openAI offers its Dots agents as part of its $100 per month ChatGPT Pro tier, and Anthropic’s Claude Duet is available with paid plans, which start at $20 per month. That makes Tasks and Meta Muse — the latter was called the “worst AI agent for privacy” by ZDNET’s David Gewirtz — Big Tech’s most affordable personal agents on the market, though you’ll have to pay for more than five hours of access at a time.

    According to recent reports, if Tasks sounds familiar, it should: The firm already has a product called Google Tasks, which lets you turn emails into a checkable to-do list on the side of your inbox, among other places like Chat and Docs. This is the agentic version, obviously.

    Gewirtz, ZDNET’s AI tester-in-residence, wasn’t blown away by then-Spark when he tried it last month, but had reason to believe in its eventual improvement. It’s unclear whether Tasks is meaningfully different from Spark, aside from being out of beta.

    In a recent development, abilities aside, what sets Tasks apart here is cost. Dots and Duet haven’t exactly impressed thus far, so free alternatives don’t have a high bar to reach yet.

    Also: I tested OpenAI Dot and Anthropic Duet for weeks.

    During Gewirtz’s test, when the agent was part of his $20 per month Google AI Pro proposal, he used only 20% of the total five hours of usage on “four fairly substantial tests.” Without an AI plan, Gemini’s context window is 32k tokens.

    At launch in September, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg noted Muse is “free to use for up to 100M tokens per week,” though Meta’s help center is not so explicit. As with most agentic products, more frequent users may want to buy more access, but more casual users now have two options to compare.

    AI companies are vying to hook customers with their various personal agents, and price and privacy are major factors to consider. Being free with limits, Muse and Tasks are perhaps geared toward a more apprehensive user who wants to try an agent, but isn’t giving it countless tasks to take on all day. Given Muse’s reputation, some may find Tasks a bit less aggressive or risky.

    Sources indicate that also: Don’t use Muse? How Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

    As with other agents, Tasks, which runs on its newest Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, can handle a variety of jobs for you, from grocery shopping to booking appointments and analyzing your heating bill. Agents like these are designed for a chronically overwhelmed society trained by a reliance on tech to seek convenience and productivity in nearly every aspect of life.

    In a recent development, the feature is free in the US, Canada, Korea, Japan, Australia, and India. US users can also start tasks by emailing or texting Gemini, and can have the agent call businesses for them (except in Indiana, Louisiana, Minnesota, Montana, and Nebraska).

    Sources indicate that the change from Spark to Tasks comes just a day after Google retired Gems (which let you tailor Gemini to specific tasks), and converted existing Gems into Skills. The latest landing page for Tasks emphasizes personal finance and cost-cutting as a use case, positioning itself alongside personal finance features from Anthropic and OpenAI.

    In a recent development, “Put Gemini on the hunt for ways to save. Identify recurring expenses you no longer need, get alerts for your most-desired deals, and more,” the page reads.

    AI agents remain a privacy and security risk, because of their ability to autonomously and proactively handle tasks like placing orders (which you can set spending caps for) and reviewing files.

    Recent findings suggest that also: Want to try ChatGPT Wallet? Read OpenAI’s liability disclaimer.

    “You can adjust task settings, disconnect Google and third-party apps, or delete chat history anytime,’ Google’s blog on the release noted. Google’s new Memory summary feature for Gemini lets users view and edit the personal info the chatbot has on them.

    • It has been revealed that if you use an AI chatbot and you’re concerned about your privacy and the personal information it ingests, you can do something about it.

    • From having Claude train on your conversations to track your location and more, here are a series of settings you should consider changing if you want to stay on top of your privacy when using one of the best AI chatbots around.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that if you use an AI chatbot and you’re concerned about your privacy and the personal information it ingests, you can do something about it. While Claude — our top pick for AI chatbots — is one of the better options when it comes to privacy, the default settings can still leave something to be desired if you value yours.

    Luckily, you can mitigate or even eliminate the amount of data Claude knows about you, as long as you know where to look.

    From having Claude train on your conversations to track your location and more, here are a series of settings you should consider changing if you want to stay on top of your privacy when using one of the best AI chatbots around.

    By default, most AI chatbots have a setting on by default that allows them to be trained on the conversations you have. This is the first and likely the most important setting you need to disable. Here’s how to turn it off.

    The settings essentially remain the same across web, iOS and Android:.

    Industry observers note that you may not see this option because with some accounts, like Enterprise prepares, Claude doesn’t automatically collect this data. So if you have a Claude account through work, you might not have to worry about this.

    While you’re at it, if you’re a Claude Code user, these settings will let you delete Code sessions stored on Anthropic’s server without deleting local sessions on your computer.

    If you’ve ever shared a chat with anyone, you can also delete those chats in this menu as well.

    Read More: Keep Your Data Yours: How to Opt Out of AI Chatbot Training.

    Anthropic will use your location when using Claude to “improve product experience.” It will use your device’s IP address to identify your city and region, but you can disable this setting — to some extent. How you go about doing this will depend on what device you’re using to access Claude.

    Industry observers note that according to the support article, if you’re using the mobile app (iOS or Android) or the web extension, the location settings are located within the device’s settings and not the Claude app settings. However, I found two ways to do this on Android. (See below.).

    The Claude app will not request access to your location unless your prompt has a specific location-based query, like “What are some of the best sushi restaurants around me?” Only then will the app request permission.

    However, if you already have given Claude access on Android or iOS, here’s how you can revoke permission.

    I was surprised to see a section in the Settings of the Android app that I didn’t see on iOS, but it will also allow you to disable your location right from the app.

    One thing to keep in mind is that turning your location off can affect features like searches that require your location, but Anthropic explicitly states that it collects your IP address to infer coarse-grained location to ensure usage of Claude complies with its terms and to prevent abuse — despite questionable allegations.

    Like other AI chatbots, Claude has built-in “memory” so it can more easily have context about your conversations. Memory is on by default: The chatbot will remember personal preferences and other information and will be able to take that into consideration in other conversations, even if you don’t explicitly mention it in your current session.

    If you’d prefer a clean slate, you can ask in the chat what memories it has collected about you and then tell Claude to delete specific memories or all of them. However, there’s a dedicated section in the settings to help you view and manage memories directly.

    In the web version of Claude, do the following to access your memory settings:.

    This will display all stored memories Claude has for you. You can edit a specific memory to your liking by clicking on the pencil icon on the right side of the memory or delete it entirely by clicking on the trash icon.

    To prevent Claude from creating newly introduced memories from your conversations:.

    If you have had conversations with Claude that were sensitive in nature and still had the “Help improve our AI models” option enabled, odds are that Anthropic has already trained Claude on that conversation. There’s no way to change that.

    However, you should find those conversations in your chat history and delete them. After you’ve done that and disabled AI training on your conversations, you should opt for incognito mode for any further sensitive conversations you might want to have going forward.

    Incognito chats aren’t saved in your history, nor are they used to train models.

    By Daniel Sparks – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:23PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Marvell Technology ›.

    Marvell Technology (MRVL -11.69%) will release results for its fiscal third quarter of 2027 (the period ended Oct. 31, 2026) on Tuesday, Dec. 1, with a conference call at 1:30 p.m. Pacific time.

    Industry observers note that the chipmaker's stock comes into the report at around $138 as I write, off about 56% from its June 4 record close of $316.43. And most of that drop is recent. Marvell shares ended Oct. 28 at around $252, the last trading day before speculation started about a deal for optical parts maker Lumentum Holdings.

    Recent findings suggest that on Nov. 2, the two companies unveiled an all-stock deal. After it closes, Marvell's current shareholders will own around two-thirds of the combined company. The growth stock is down about 45% from that Oct. 28 close.

    In a recent development, the Dec. 1 report will be Marvell's first full quarterly revision since it agreed to buy Lumentum. And if the past three years are any guide, the shares might make a massive move the day after.

    Industry observers note that matt Murphy. Image source: Getty Images.

    According to recent reports, marvell reports after the market closes, so the reaction shows up in the next day's trading. Here are its last 12 reports, the stock's close-to-close move the next day, and the revenue growth management guided for the following quarter over the quarter just reported.

    Industry observers note that data source: Yahoo Finance and Marvell. Calculations by author.

    Shares dropped the next day seven times and climbed five times.

    It has been revealed that and the moves were big either way. The average swing was around 12%, and seven of the 12 moves topped 10%.

    Interestingly, the quarters themselves were almost never to blame. In all 12 reports, Marvell's revenue came in above the midpoint of its guidance.

    Recent findings suggest that I think the outlook mattered more. In the six reports in which management guided to next-quarter revenue growth of 6% or lower (with one guide for a decline), the stock fell the next day five times, with an average drop of around 9%.

    In the six where it guided for about 8% or more, shares climbed four times, with an average gain of about 6%.

    Industry observers note that but six reports on either side doesn't prove much, and the pattern has a clear exception. In August 2026, management guided to third-quarter revenue of $3.15 billion, up 15% from the second quarter's $2.74 billion, the second-largest increase in the table. The stock still dropped 10% the next day.

    A possible reason is that expectations had risen with the tech firm's share price, which had more than tripled since the March 2026 report.

    It has been revealed that this time, the quarter itself could hold even less surprise than normal. When it declared the Lumentum deal on Nov. 2, Marvell mentioned preliminary third-quarter revenue was in line with its guidance. It kept the $3.15 billion midpoint and tightened the range to plus or minus 2%.

    It has been revealed that that puts the focus on the fiscal fourth quarter, and the bar is high for a chipmaker helped by demand for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. Marvell's revenue climbed 22% year over year in the final quarter of fiscal 2026. Growth then rose to 28% and 37% in the first two quarters of fiscal 2027. And the $3.15 billion third-quarter midpoint means growth of around 52%, an acceleration for a third straight quarter.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    "[W]e expect our revenue growth to accelerate further through the remainder of fiscal 2027," Marvell CEO Matt Murphy said in the manufacturer's fiscal second-quarter earnings release.

    For growth to keep accelerating in the fiscal fourth quarter, revenue would have to exceed $3.4 billion, or about 7% above the third-quarter midpoint. In other words, a guide that just keeps pace with the third quarter might land right around the line that has split the stock's past reactions.

    Sources indicate that in the end, I'd expect a big move on Dec. 2 either way, and a down day has been a bit more common than an up day. But I wouldn't read much into one day's move when the Lumentum deal isn't expected to close until the first half of 2028.

    In a recent development, personally, I'd pay more attention to the size of the fourth-quarter guide than to the stock's reaction to it. Shares trade at around 20 times the earnings analysts expect for fiscal 2028, a price that seems reasonable if growth continues to accelerate. And if shares drop again on a guide that still shows accelerating growth, I think the lower price might be worth considering for investors who can ride out more swings like these.

    #27875. I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

    I Didn’t Know Southwest Points Could Be This Valuable

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1659 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that in a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary.
    • Industry observers note that take Southwest Airlines, for example.
    • "Experiences create lifetime memories,” indicates Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that in a world of transferable points currencies, you might not think holding an airline or hotel credit card is necessary. But travel brands are pushing back against that narrative, offering exclusive perks and redemption packages to those who carry their cards.

    Industry observers note that take Southwest Airlines, for example. Its Rapid Rewards loyalty program allows you to redeem points for flights, but it also offers a special program called Rapid Rewards Access Events exclusively for Southwest credit cardholders. In exchange for a decent chunk of points, you can get a vacation package that’s worth significantly more than the price you pay. Instead of a traditional flight award redemption, you get a cohesive travel experience.

    "Experiences create lifetime memories,” indicates Nandika Suri, Southwest’s vice president of Rapid Rewards. “For us, we really want them to have great memories and remember our brand as part of that.”.

    Industry observers note that southwest invited me to participate in one of its Rapid Rewards Access Events. While Southwest covered the cost of my trip, these opinions are my own. Here’s what I learned.

    Every event is different (ranging from concerts to multiday trips), but significant-ticket Rapid Rewards Access Events tend to include flights, hotel accommodations, meals and excursions.

    According to recent reports, the event I participated in was in Maui to celebrate the 30th anniversary of Southwest and Chase’s partnership. This was a bigger production than the typical event, with about 60 cardholders (and a plus one) participating. A typical multiday event might have 20 or 25 packages for sale.

    In exchange for 275,000 Rapid Rewards points, cardholders received for themselves and one guest:.

    A four-night stay in an ocean-view room at the Grand Wailea, a Waldorf Astoria Resort, in Maui, including daily breakfast.

    Ground transportation between the airport and the resort, as well as for any scheduled group activities.

    A special welcome reception and farewell dinner.

    A snorkeling cruise with lunch and beverages included.

    A choice between several excursions, including a spa treatment, golf, ziplining and more.

    Even at extremely conservative estimates, I would value all of those things at roughly $4,600. That’s $750 more than what NerdWallet values 275,000 Rapid Rewards points at, according to our 2026 data. If we took a more liberal approach, I think it would be fair to say the package was worth more than $7,000. That puts this redemption between 1.7 and 2.5 cents per point. (Expand the section below to see how I arrived at those numbers.).

    As of 2026, NerdWallet values Southwest Rapid Rewards points at 1.4 cents apiece. That puts the 275,000-point Southwest event package at $3,850.

    Let’s put some numbers to the package inclusions and see how the points price stacks up to the cash valuation.

    According to recent reports, $1,000 Southwest gift card: It’s pretty easy to value a $1,000 Southwest gift card at $1,000. You need to fly to the event, so that can be taken at face value. (You could also use it toward a different trip, if you wanted to use points or fly with a different carrier.).

    Four-night hotel stay: For the Grand Wailea stay, a nonrefundable Hilton Honors discount rate for an ocean-view room on the exact same dates in 2027 costs $4,490.19, after factoring in taxes and fees. (The base-level terrace-view room would cost $3,992.17.).

    It has been revealed that if you were to use points, a standard room without an ocean view would cost 130,000 Hilton points per night. An ocean-view room’s rate shoots up to 281,000 Hilton points per night.

    According to recent reports, using NerdWallet’s 2026 valuation of Hilton points at 0.4 cent per point, that puts the value of the two rooms at $2,080 and $4,496, respectively. To make things interesting, let’s say the hotel stay is worth $2,080.

    Daily breakfast at the hotel buffet is about $60 per person, before tax and tip. For four days, let’s put that at around another $500, bringing the total stay value to $2,580.

    Ground transportation: Let’s make things simple and just say it’s $30 each way between the airport and the resort. For two people, that would be worth $120.

    Welcome reception and farewell dinner: Southwest and Chase put a lot of effort into making these events nice, from the food and free-flowing alcohol to the entertainment (there was even a fire performance at the farewell dinner).

    I would value this at $50 per person, conservatively, or $200 total.

    Snorkeling cruise: I went on Viator to find a similar experience, and the cheapest option I found was priced at $100 per person.

    Recent findings suggest that again, let’s price it conservatively and say it’s worth $200. That price doesn't include hotel transportation, gratuities, towels or alcoholic beverages, while the Southwest package did.

    Excursion choice: Southwest let everyone choose an excursion, ranging from a chill pool or spa day to ziplining through the jungle or learning to surf.

    It’s hard to put a number on this, because the activities varied in cost.

    Industry observers note that I went ziplining, and it was $240 for six lines. That price doesn’t include transportation to the excursion, which was covered by Southwest. Meanwhile, a standard massage at the hotel spa is $275 (and that doesn’t even factor in the 20% service charge).

    Let’s put this at $250 per person, giving us a round $500 for two people’s excursions.

    Grand total: Summing up these numbers gets us $4,600. That’s $750 more than the $3,850 NerdWallet values 275,000 points at, but keep in mind that we probably undervalued several of the inclusions. The actual value of a trip like this could be much higher.

    It also doesn’t factor in other things, like snacks provided at the hospitality booth, as well as surprise gifts and goodie bags prepared by Southwest and Chase for attendees.

    Before you book a Rapid Rewards Access Event, there are some drawbacks to booking a vacation this way.

    It has been revealed that the biggest one is if you don’t like group trips or following a schedule on your vacations. Given the nature of these events, you’ll be surrounded by a group of travelers, many of whom will likely be longtime Southwest flyers. If you prefer to keep to yourself, then this type of trip is likely not a good fit.

    According to recent reports, you’ll also have multiple scheduled activities on your itinerary. While you can choose to not show up, those activities add a lot of value to the trip.

    It has been revealed that with that remarked, I found the itinerary quite laid back. The amount of scheduled activities wasn’t overwhelming, and there was plenty of free time to do whatever you wanted. One couple I met even rented a car and explored Maui in their downtime, so they kept themselves busy.

    These events are extremely popular, and many attendees I met at the Maui event had been on multiple Southwest cardmember trips.

    Industry observers note that scoring a ticket to a Rapid Rewards Access Event might even require setting your alarm for when tickets drop. Several cardmembers told me they’ve experienced times when the event they wanted was sold out in hours, if not minutes. (The Maui one took a few hours to sell out, because it was larger than most.).

    Recent findings suggest that finally, 275,000 points is a lot — even if you're getting great value. If your Rapid Rewards points are collecting dust in your account, then it could make sense. But if you have a transferable currency, then you'd have to weigh whether you might get better value elsewhere, such as booking round-trip business class flights.

    Southwest isn’t the only airline or travel brand to offer special events for cardholders. United Airlines has MileagePlus Exclusives and United Card Events from Chase; Delta Air Lines offers cardmember-exclusive redemptions in its SkyMiles Experiences program; and Marriott has its Marriott Bonvoy Moments program.

    But every redemption option is different — even if it’s within the same loyalty program. For example, some Rapid Rewards Access Events are packages you can purchase immediately for a set price, while others are auction-style listings. Some programs offer paid experiences, so you can only pay in cash, not points.

    Sources indicate that personally, I’m a fan of the fixed-price points option. You know the upfront price, and you don’t have to worry about getting into a last-minute bidding war that could lead you to paying more than you intended. Plus, Southwest has historically had limited award redemption options, although that will change in 2027 when it allows international partner award bookings.

    Ultimately, whether you think a Rapid Rewards Access Event is a worthwhile redemption will depend on your interests, and Southwest is working to expand its offerings to meet people’s passions.

    "We do offer a lot of breadth because we want to get different types of customers engaged with different types of things based on their individual passion points and what they're really interested in,” says Suri, the Rapid Rewards chief.

    If you’d rather spend time in the mountains than on the beach, you might not want to spend 275,000 Rapid Rewards points on the Maui package.

    Instead, you probably would've been interested in the 250,000-point package for "Boots, Bourbon and Bonfires" — a three-day trip to Devil's Thumb Ranch, an upscale dude ranch resort about 1.5 hours outside of Denver.

    Before you book, just remember: You’ll need a Southwest credit card to purchase.

    In a recent development, you want a travel credit card that prioritizes what’s important to you. Here are some of the best travel credit cards of 2026:.

    No annual fee: Wells Fargo Autograph® Card.

    Bonus travel rewards and high-end perks: Chase Sapphire Reserve®.

    Luxury perks: American Express Platinum Card®.

    Business travelers: Ink Business Preferred® Credit Card.

    Google Wallet comes to your iPhone – but without this feature

    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone owners in the US for the first time.
    • Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.
    • Recent findings suggest that the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Google Wallet app is available for iPhone owners in the US for the first time. iOS users who download the fresh Google Wallet app can manage online payments for faster checkout at places that support Google Pay. However, Apple restricts Google’s ability to offer tap-to-pay service on the iOS app, so users won’t be able to use Google Wallet for contactless checkout on iPhone.

    Also: You can use Google’s Spark AI agent, renamed Tasks, for free now – with limits.

    Recent findings suggest that the fresh Google Wallet app lets you digitize physical cards, including payment, loyalty, and membership cards, as well as boarding passes. Google Wallet app customers on iOS will also be able to view receipts and track orders pulled from Gmail in one app.

    There used to be a Google Pay app for iOS, but it was discontinued in 2024. The old Google Pay app also didn’t support tap-to-pay on iPhone, but it offered limited functionality, including support for loyalty and gift cards, as well as purchase tracking.

    The biggest difference between the old Google Pay app for iOS and the new Google Wallet is the AI component, which supports agentic shopping, likely as Google’s longer-term play.

    One of Google’s goals for the Wallet app on iOS is to make it a central place to manage purchases made by its AI agents. The Agents section in Google Wallet for iPhone lets you manage and monitor purchases made through Gemini.

    Agentic commerce is on the rise, as evidenced by the growing use of Meta’s Muse. Gemini can make purchases and payments through the Tasks feature, which lets you give Gemini permission to buy the items you want and set your maximum budget.

    Also: Google Wallet just turned your Android phone into a digital house key.

    According to recent reports, the Google Wallet app for iOS becomes the central hub for purchase management in agentic commerce through Gemini. In it, you can view active tasks to see which purchases Gemini is working on, as well as completed purchases and receipts.

    Google has been working on two technologies to support its agentic commerce strategy: Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) and Agent Payments Protocol (AP2).

    UCP is a technical language that enables AI agents to communicate with retailers and make purchases, while AP2 is the payment framework that establishes rules and authorization for agents to make payments.

    Google Wallet serves as both the AI-powered wallet and the consumer-facing record of transactions made by Gemini.

    Also: Google Wallet has a lot of upcoming tricks – these 5 are my favorites.

    Along with Google, major retailers supported the development of UCP, including Shopify, Walmart, Target, and Etsy. When Google declared AP2, more than 60 organizations became involved, including PayPal, Salesforce, Mastercard, and American Express.

    Meta’s Carbon Emissions Went Up 45% Last Year. AI Is Making It Worse

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used.
    • In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the organization is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.
    • It’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, meta promised to be carbon-neutral and water-positive by 2030 — that is, the company would offset as much carbon dioxide as it created and return more water to local watersheds than it used. But like every Substantial Tech company, Meta is sacrificing its climate goals for artificial intelligence and the data centers needed to run it.

    In Meta’s 2026 sustainability report, released on Thursday, Meta’s data center and sustainability chiefs wrote that the organization is “re-evaluating our timelines, sequencing, and interim milestones — including the 2030 timeframe for our net zero emissions goal and our near-term intensity targets.” In an emailed statement to CNET, a Meta spokesperson added, “We remain committed to net zero, but are re-evaluating the 2030 timeline … We’ll continue to invest in emissions reductions.”.

    It’s a disappointing, if unsurprising, announcement. Microsoft, Amazon and Google have also all backtracked on their climate goals in their rush to build hyperscale data centers, the turbocharged server farms needed to keep AI online. Microsoft’s president, Brad Smith, noted in 2023 that the tech giant’s net zero goal was “before the explosion in artificial intelligence.”.

    Meta’s net emissions in 2025 were 11.8 million metric tons of carbon dioxide, a 45% increase year over year, the firm states. Carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gases are primary drivers of the climate crisis, worsening natural disasters, causing more extreme weather patterns and disrupting the lives of everyone and everything on the planet.

    It has been revealed that take one of Meta’s Louisiana data centers, Hyperion, for example. CEO Mark Zuckerberg announced the behemoth in 2025, showing how the facility is nearly the size of Manhattan. When it comes online in 2030, it’s expected to create two gigawatts of capacity for AI, with the ability to scale in the future. But it also requires equally massive demands on the state’s energy grid.

    Meta details in length its strategies for mitigating the environmental impact of its work, including improved water-use efficiencies in its data centers and approximately 77% less embodied carbon in its new data center designs compared to its original ones.

    But, again, AI has made an indelible mark on those efforts. The company also reports that its electricity consumption “increased 35% year over year as additional data centers came online.”.

    Meta wrote that “demand for AI infrastructure has grown faster than almost anyone projected.” Arguably, as one of the biggest hyperscalers driving the buildout of AI infrastructure here in the US and abroad, Meta should have known.

    #27870. 90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1071 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Zdnet ↗ Open Full Page

    90% of employers reject resumes that look like AI – yet half use AI to interview

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1071 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider.
    • New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.
    • Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Hiring managers are more suspicious than ever of AI use in applications, and it’s impacting who they consider. At the same time, they’re turning to AI to help screen more candidates — meaning those videos you’ve seen on the internet of people pranking AI interviewers aren’t going away anytime soon.

    New data from hiring systems firm Greenhouse found that “nine in ten US employers (90%) believe they’ve turned away real candidates because those applications seemed fake or AI-generated.” Greenhouse clarified that it doesn’t know whether employers are putting applications through AI detection tools or not.

    Also: How many jobs is your state losing to AI? This dashboard tracks the cuts – and the cost.

    “The survey data is self-reported, so it reflects what employers believe has happened, not a measured outcome,” Greenhouse’s Head of Voice AI Ophir Samson told ZDNET via email.

    Industry observers note that employers are also reacting to AI by adjusting their hiring processes: 86% of those surveyed reported changes to account for AI’s impact. 57% of them did so by adding another human interview.

    “As jobseekers rely more on AI to polish and send out their job applications, employers are finding it harder to tell who’s actually right for the role,” the report stated, echoing an ongoing push-and-pull between applicants and hiring teams. AI resume screeners automatically toss a majority of applications they deem unfit, so applicants try not to get tossed by formatting their material for the screener, which then backfires anyway.

    Sources indicate that the report demonstrates how a tough economy and an influx of AI hiring tools are colliding, arguably to benefit employers over applicants. Greenhouse noted that, ironically, AI tools are helping hiring managers while also making resumes untrustworthy, and applicants would rather be interviewed by AI than not at all.

    Also: How to beat the AI algorithm and get the job of your dreams.

    “A growing number of employers are using AI not just to filter candidates out, but to have conversations with more candidates, earlier, through AI-powered voice technology,” Greenhouse stated, adding that “half now use AI interviews to hear from more candidates, and 40% of those have found strong candidates they would have missed.”.

    According to recent reports, greenhouse itself offers a voice AI screening interview tool. Samson told ZDNET that an HR professional ran 200 candidates she’d rejected through Greenhouse’s tool, and it suggested 19.

    “All five of the finalists came from that group, and she ultimately hired one from the group,” Samson said.

    It has been revealed that what we don’t, and maybe can’t, know is the inverse: whether AI screeners influence hiring managers to turn away candidates they actually should have considered. At least in Greenhouse’s case, Samson mentioned Voice AI doesn’t make hiring decisions or “automatically advance, reject, or rank candidates.”.

    “Recruiters review every output, and one recruiter owns the outcome and can explain how they reached it,” he said.

    Greenhouse’s report surveyed 1,347 hiring managers and recruiters across the US, UK, Germany, Australia, and Ireland from late September to mid-October, and found that half of employers using voice AI “say the early-stage candidate experience has improved.”.

    Also: ‘So perfect, they are literally identical’ – Your AI-polished resumes are recruiters’ latest top stressor.

    It’s unclear what “improved” means there, though, and whether applicants themselves would agree with that. Still, when given the choice, only 7% of applicants in the US would turn down an AI interview, per an earlier Greenhouse report. Additionally, “70% of those who’ve had a live AI interview say it helped them show their skills,” that report said.

    But how swayed is that by the state of the US job market? October’s job report was better than expected, but it’s still been a tough year overall for job-seekers. Greenhouse’s findings could be as much a reflection of how desperate applicants are as an endorsement of or comfort with AI screenings.

    “The job market could be a factor. Our Future of Hiring Candidate Report demonstrates 81% of job seekers were rejected from a job in the past year without speaking to anyone at the company, human or AI,” Samson mentioned. “But I’d be careful about reading the data as desperation. Candidates are setting clear conditions: nearly half (49%) want to know if a human will review their responses and 40% want to know how they’ll be evaluated.”.

    Also: Why replacing staff with AI backfires – and 5 ways smart leaders generate real value instead.

    According to recent reports, samson said that a software engineer named Ryan Quinlan, who was hired at Blissway, initially thought “talking to an AI” sounded stranger, but that it ultimately “felt like a conversation” that let him mention skills he’d forgotten to include on his resume. Samson said that Ryan has been “a ‘maybe’ on paper,” but that the AI interview helped him get over the line to be considered.

    “For most applicants, a human conversation was never on the table,” Samson remarked. “The real choice is a resume lost in a pile, or 15 minutes to tell their story.”.

    Greenhouse found that while employers are using AI to screen more candidates, most are maintaining human oversight over the most vital decisions in the hiring process.

    “Of all the tasks employers would hand to an AI agent, deciding which candidates to advance came last, at just 7%,” Greenhouse said.

    It has been revealed that A recent California law aims to protect employees from being fired by AI systems that make determinations about their performance without a human co-signing the assessment. As with many AI productivity tools in the workplace, proper adoption ideally equates to more time for human workers to handle more notable tasks.

    Also: 92% of HR say staff can train for AI jobs – but half of companies still hire outside.

    “Of employers who’ve saved time with AI, 85% put it back into candidates, most often by spending more time with shortlisted candidates (45%) and interviewing more candidates earlier (40%),” Greenhouse noted.

    The main question around AI interviewers remains whether they’re correctly capturing your interview the way you’d hope a human interviewer would (though that’s still deeply subjective and out of applicants’ control anyway).

    In a recent development, “When AI interviews are implemented thoughtfully and transparently, they pay off for both candidates and recruiters,” Samson said. “Every candidate who uses our Voice AI can opt out, and about 90% rate the experience as excellent.”.

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (595 w)

    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Signal Is Blocking Screenshots to Protect Your Messages from AI Agents

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (595 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message.
    • The privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a fresh default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data.
    • That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that don’t ask your AI agent to read and decipher that lengthy text message. And don’t screenshot it either. It may seem harmless, but Signal’s latest setting underlines that it isn’t.

    The privacy-focused messaging and calling app is rolling out a fresh default setting to stop built-in smartphone AI agents from potentially seeing and saving your Signal data. In a blog post announcing the change, Signal President Meredith Whittaker said these AI bots scan what’s on your screen to get to know you, capturing your data and making it available to AI systems to fulfill your requests, such as answering questions you may ask.

    That threatens Signal’s mission to guarantee privacy, Whittaker wrote. So it’s putting a stop to it with a default setting to block screenshots in the Signal app on iOS 27 and when AI assistants try to capture information on Android screens by default.

    Whittaker stated that this isn’t the first time Signal has taken such measures against an operating system. Last year, it blocked screenshots of Signal messages from Microsoft’s Recall AI on Windows 11.

    Now the company is taking a similar approach to Apple’s iOS 27 and Android operating systems, where AI assistants try to read your Signal screen.

    The problem is the same for the three major OS companies. Microsoft, Google and Apple are incorporating AI into their operating systems, and Signal says that compromises the space for third-party developers, including Signal, to build apps for these systems.

    “Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that’s making it increasingly hostile to privacy,” Whittaker wrote.

    Whittaker noted the screenshot setting won’t fix everything, because AI agents can still sneakily access data on your phone. Tech companies should take steps to give developers more choice, such as an opt-out to disable AI agent access, and provide more documentation on how significant tech AI agents work.

    Sources indicate that “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience,” Whittaker said. “This is also the reason we are presently unable to implement these protections on MacOS.”.

    In most cases, text messages are encrypted when they travel between devices. But AI agents can bypass that. John Strand, CEO of Black Hills Information Security, explained that when you access the information, it has to be decrypted because you cannot read encrypted data.

    “So, if an AI agent can access screenshots or directly observe what’s happening on your screen, it can read those messages without ever having to break the encryption itself,” noted Strand. “That’s the scary part. You can have incredibly strong encryption, but if something can see what the user sees, that encryption isn’t going to protect you at that point.”.

    If you want to take screenshots in Signal, you can disable the setting, but that could mean AI agents could access you and your senders’ information, like text messages and shared files such as photos.

    According to recent reports, strand remarked the worst-case scenario is that an attacker could see everything you see, from private conversations to passwords. And that’s what Signal is trying to avoid.

    “They want to make sure that if something like this happens, they’ve done absolutely everything they reasonably can to protect their customers and the information being accessed through their application,” Strand said.

    Signal, Apple and Google did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
