    Breaking: The Flipper One is more than a Zero 2.0 – it’s a $399 Linux computer with a $13M Kickstarter

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (716 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero.
    • Recent findings suggest that the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use.
    • Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Flipper One crowdfunding campaign has broken the $13-million mark, smashing the funding raised for previous Flipper devices and demonstrating strong interest in the successor to the Flipper Zero. The $399 Flipper One is a pocket Linux computer focused on networking, with delivery estimated for July 2027. But it isn’t simply an updated version of the Flipper Zero. It’s a very different animal and a much more serious bit of kit.

    Recent findings suggest that the thing that made the Flipper Zero so popular was how easy it was to use. You could fire it up and turn the volume down on the TV at your parents’ place, see the radio waves coming from your car’s key fob, and copy hotel room key cards.

    Also: The Flipper One may be the ultimate Linux PC for hackers in 2026 – and I’m excited.

    It could do a lot, there wasn’t a steep learning curve, and you didn’t need to buy anything else. Did the fake videos on TikTok from people claiming they could change the prices at gas stations (I wish!) or start cars remotely help make the Zero more popular?

    Industry observers note that unfortunately, yes. But what made it successful was that it packed a lot of power into a package that was small, fun, affordable, and easy to use.

    If the Flipper Zero, with its NFC, RFID, sub-GHz, and IR, was kindergarten, the Flipper One is a college degree: a pocket Linux computer focused on networking.

    Recent findings suggest that this is reflected in the price. You can pick up a Zero for $169, while the Flipper One is $399.

    What this buys you is the Flipper One base computer with a 256 × 144 grayscale LCD, Rockchip RK3576 8-core ARM SoC with NPU, a low-power MCU for handling the LCD and user interface, 8GB of LPDDR5 RAM, 64GB of UFS 2.2 storage, and a microSD slot.

    If that $399 feels like a lot, it’s worth keeping in mind that, according to Flipper, the price only covers production costs and that the RAM and UFS storage account for at least half of the total hardware cost.

    If you think this is a lot, you could spend a lot more. Adding a LoRa, SDR, or 5G module will push the total up a lot higher. And if you want all three modules, you’re looking at $759 for the Flipper One Ultimate Bundle.

    Also: The Flipper One is the Linux cyberdeck I wish my Raspberry Pi could be.

    Recent findings suggest that the reception has been strong enough that pledges have flown past the $300,000 goal that Flipper initially set, with over 24,000 backers pledging over $13 million. Close to 5,300 backers have gone for the Ultimate Bundle, compared to just over 4,300 choosing the bare Flipper One.

    This suggests that backers really want the radio capabilities that this new platform offers.

    If you want one, this crowdfunding run is a good time to get one because it’s a Kickstarter Special slashing 25% off an estimated retail price of $550.

    The response over on Reddit has been a little more subdued, with some being taken aback by the price of the Zero’s bigger sibling.

    Also: 7 useful things I can do with my Flipper Zero – as someone who’s used it for years.

    As someone who homebrews a lot of electronics, I’m going to say that the price is justified, and this project goes far beyond something you could put together with a Raspberry Pi and some code.

    Industry observers note that the Flipper One campaign runs until Dec. 17, 2026, with delivery estimated for July 2027.

    Keep in mind that this is a Kickstarter pledge, not a purchase, and that rewards aren’t guaranteed. Flipper also states on the Kickstarter page that component shortages are the biggest risk to the project and that they “could cause significant delays to production and delivery.” It also says that if RAM prices continue to rise, it cannot “rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.”.

    Also: Is the Flipper Zero the best multi-tool for hacking?

    And the good news here is that I’ve seen several analysts predicting that RAM prices will begin to go down in 2027 as demand eases off.

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1069 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    What to Buy (and Skip) on Black Friday 2026

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1069 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month.
    • If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines!
    • It has been revealed that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, black Friday comes but once a year — although sometimes it feels like it lasts for a month. The big day is Nov. 27, but the sales have already started.

    If you’ve been sitting on a holiday shopping list and waiting for prices to drop, we’ve got good news: It’s time to start your shopping engines! (So to speak.).

    It has been revealed that you don’t need a calendar full of sale dates to navigate the shopping frenzy. Focus on the categories likely to offer the biggest savings. Here’s what to buy, and what can wait.

    If you’ve got top-priority toys on your list, buy them at a discount if you can find them, claims Kristin McGrath, senior editor at The Krazy Coupon Lady, “just in case they don’t go down in price later.”.

    Sources indicate that non-electronic toys are a good bet, states Julie Ramhold, consumer analyst with DealNews.com, because they’re less affected by tariffs on electronic components. That includes Legos, dolls and playsets.

    According to recent reports, neeDoh squishies are a hot stocking stuffer this year and may be in short supply. At authorized retailers like Target, they should be relatively affordable, but try to avoid unauthorized resellers who may crank up the price, Ramhold says.

    While you may see mattress stores offering a few doorbusters on Black Friday, don’t feel pressured to jump on a deal.

    In a recent development, “Mattresses tend to see some of their strongest discounts around major sales events like Labor Day and Presidents Day,” says Ashley Feinstein Gerstley, shopping and savings strategist with Rakuten. “So if you’re not in a rush, it may be worth waiting for one of those windows.”.

    Similarly, bedding and towels are often on deep discount during January white sales, Feinstein Gerstley says.

    Got some counter space and an itch for a latest food processor? Black Friday sales are a great time to price surf for countertop appliances, including blenders, juicers and air fryers.

    “Those things we see sometimes half off or more,” McGrath says. “And they’re all on sale at the same time, so any one you’re looking for is likely to have a discount.”.

    Holiday decor is only a must-buy during Black Friday sales if you need it for this holiday season.

    While you’ll still see sales on holiday items like artificial trees, drinkware and garlands, “if you can wait until after Christmas, that’s when discounts should reach up to 80% or more at stores like Target, Walmart and department stores like JCPenney and Macy’s,” Ramhold states.

    It has been revealed that electronics are typically a slam-dunk buy at this time of year. “Every store is competing for your business, so televisions, headphones, tablets, laptops — they’re all going to be on sale at the same time,” McGrath says.

    Gaming consoles, in particular, see some of the better discounts. And they often come bundled with a gift card, gaming accessories or video games. “Consoles are common gifts,” McGrath says. “The stores know that, so they’re offering competitive deals.”.

    That mentioned, the traditional deep discounts you usually see on electronics for Black Friday may be a little lackluster this year due to high prices on parts, Ramhold notes.

    Recent findings suggest that for best results, research the exact specs of the product you want and put it in your cart ahead of time, claims consumer savings expert Andrea Woroch. That way, if a similar (but not identical) product goes on sale, you won’t accidentally buy the wrong thing.

    You’ll usually find deeper discounts on items that are associated with fitness resolutions after Fresh Year’s Day.

    “Substantial-box retailers like Target and department stores like Macy’s will offer up to 40% off or more on both fitness equipment and activewear during early January sales,” Ramhold claims.

    It has been revealed that many fashion retailers offer Black Friday sales, McGrath says. So if there’s an item you stock in multiple colors or a work staple you need to replace, keep an eye on your favorite sites for the markdowns.

    Shoes, too, are a category to eyeball, including seasonal buys and everyday options like running shoes, Ramhold says. “Some retailers may offer a BOGO promotion of some kind, but it’ll likely just be a ‘buy one, get one for 50% off,’” she says.

    Just shop early for your size and color before inventory runs low, McGrath notes. “You don’t want to miss out if there's a great deal.”.

    In a recent development, one caveat: Winter apparel will usually see bigger discounts toward the end of the year, Woroch indicates. So wait on your boot and coat purchases if you can.

    Black Friday also offers the chance to snag deals on things you can use throughout the year:.

    Photo gifts: Whether you’re ordering holiday cards or putting together a photo book for your in-laws (or yourself), you can usually find sales from vendors like Snapfish and Shutterfly, among others.

    It has been revealed that fitness classes: Try your local gym, yoga or Pilates studio for discounts on class packs. “I’ll buy a 20-class package, and it’s always a great deal,” Woroch claims.

    Spa services: Check local businesses for deals on massages, manicures and other self-care treatments.

    Streaming subscriptions: If you’re a new customer (or canceled at least a month ago), some streaming platforms offer deep Black Friday discounts.

    Black Friday deals are as much about strategy as savings, so make sure you’re maximizing your spending with these tips:.

    Recent findings suggest that let AI help. Tools like ChatGPT and Gemini can do a lot of the legwork for you. Write out a product name and try prompts like “Find the lowest price for X product by comparing every retail site that it’s sold on and including coupons and cash back offers,” Woroch notes. (Just note that AI searches can be limited and may not find every deal available.).

    Sources indicate that check the price, not just the percentage: “Sometimes the base price is inflated or it was listed initially for a higher price,” Feinstein Gerstley indicates. “Another retailer might have the same item for less, even if their discount doesn't look as impressive.”.

    Use a browser extension or cash-back app. As long as you’re spending money, recapture some of it with a browser extension or cash-back app that sends a percentage of your purchase back to you.

    #27866. Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Officially Heading to Mars

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (769 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Are We There Yet? NASA’s Escapade Is Officially Heading to Mars

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that NASA released its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars.
    • Industry observers note that it’s an exciting time for NASA.
    • Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet or the sun’s natural gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that NASA released its Escapade mission just over a year ago to send two spacecraft, nicknamed Blue and Gold, to Mars. After spending a year looping near Earth, the twin probes completed a gravity-assist maneuver this month and are now en route to the red planet.

    Industry observers note that it’s an exciting time for NASA. Blue and Gold, named for the school colors of UC Berkeley where they were built, completed the agency’s first powered Earth flyby.

    Recent findings suggest that typically, spacecraft use a planet or the sun’s natural gravity to get close to the planet before slingshotting off into the distance. A notable example is Voyager 1, which used unpowered gravity-assisted flybys to reach the speeds needed to cross the light-day threshold earlier this week. Escapade did this with Earth’s gravity but also used thrusters to generate even more speed. Since there are two of them, NASA personnel had to perform this maneuver twice.

    The other substantial win for NASA is that Mars will soon have two additional satellites in orbit to measure the planet’s magnetosphere, which is believed to have been stripped by the solar wind eons ago, when the planet likely had liquid water.

    It has been revealed that these satellites are notable for being NASA’s first low-cost mission to Mars, costing the agency approximately $75 million as part of the Small Innovative Missions for Planetary Exploration program. It also marked the official debut of Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket for a space mission, and the manufacturer was able to achieve the first vertical landing of its rocket after sending Escapade on its way.

    Escapade still has a long way to go. Blue and Gold are now spending the next 10 months flying into outer space. Their new trajectory is set to take them into Mars’ orbital path, timed in such a way that the twin satellites will arrive at the same time that Mars naturally demonstrates up, allowing the red planet to capture the twins in its orbit as it flies by. NASA says that both are set to arrive at Mars by early September next year.

    By the time the twins get there, they will have been in space for 22 months. Flights to Mars require months of deep space travel, impeccable timing and loads of fuel. However, if missions hit specific launch windows, they require far less fuel.

    It has been revealed that this is a well-documented maneuver known as the Hohmann Transfer, and NASA’s JPL has a neat math exercise to show how it’s calculated. NASA intentionally released Escapade a year early so that the satellites could hang out in a gravitational sweet spot called the L2 Earth-Sun Lagrange point. This is a point in space on the side of the Earth opposite the sun, and the idea was to have the spacecraft already in orbit and ready for the next Mars launch window.

    Once it opened, the satellites engaged their thrusters, performed a gravity-assisted flyby of Earth to gain speed, and released themselves into outer space.

    The tactic of sending Escapade to the L2 Lagrange point to wait for a Mars window to open is arguably NASA’s biggest win, as no space agency has ever attempted it. The benefit is that it allows agencies to launch payloads into orbit bound for Mars whenever they have the time, then use Earth gravity assists to slingshot them out to Mars when it’s most efficient.

    Recent findings suggest that “With this loiter orbit and Earth flyby, Escapade is pioneering a latest strategy for getting to Mars,” Jeff Parker, CTO of Advanced Space and lead mission designer, remarked in a statement. “This method provides the flexibility to launch almost anytime and then use Earth’s gravity to get a boost to Mars, rather than waiting every two years to launch there directly when the planets are aligned.”.

    The maneuver paid dividends. JAXA, Japan’s national space agency, debuted its MMX spacecraft on Oct. 20, which is within the current Mars launch window and employs the same Hohmann Transfer method to get to Mars. The spacecraft is headed to Phobos and Deimos, Mars’s moons.

    In a recent development, despite using the more traditional method of waiting for the window to open to launch, JAXA’s MMX is slated to reach its destination in August next year, just a couple of weeks ahead of Escapade. When you factor in that Escapade performed its gravity-assist slingshot on Nov. 9, roughly two weeks before MMX debuted, the spacecraft will reach their respective destinations in approximately the same amount of time, validating NASA’s trajectory strategy.

    Industry observers note that most of the major AIs offer a temporary chat or incognito option in which your conversation remains private and vanishes as soon as your chat ends. Now Google has jumped on board this bandwagon with its AI Mode searches.

    Also: Google is making it easier to opt out of Gemini AI training.

    Recent findings suggest that new to Google’s AI Mode is an option known as temporary threads. By choosing this setting, any searches you conduct in AI mode are detached from your own Google account and history. Your temporary searches won’t be affected by your past preferences or chats. They won’t be impacted by any personalization you’ve set up through your account. And they won’t be saved to your chat history. The goal here is to prevent anyone else, including Google, from accessing your conversations in this mode.

    In a recent development, this option is presently rolling out around the world in all languages to Google search on both desktop and mobile browsers. You can run a temporary thread on any device and in any browser.

    Try this for yourself: Head to the regular Google search page and click the button on the search field for AI Mode. You should then see an icon with a pen hovering over a dotted circle. If you don’t see it, you may have to run a search to get started. On the results page, you should then spot the icon.

    According to recent reports, hover over the icon, and the tooltip will say: “Start temporary thread.” Click the icon on the left to start a new thread. Now, any conversation you kick off will be temporary and unconnected to your account. But you don’t have to stick with just plain old text. Select the plus icon to upload an image or file. Select the microphone icon to speak instead of type.

    Also: Goodbye, Gemini Gems: How to use Google’s latest Skills.

    Certain limitations are in effect with a temporary thread. Specifically, you can’t do any of the following:.

    It has been revealed that are these temporary threads truly private? Here’s what Google notes:.

    Sources indicate that “Temporary threads will not be saved to your Google account and disappear after 24 hours,” Google said on a support page. “They won’t be used to train Google’s generative AI models, unless you submit feedback or it’s necessary for safety purposes. Google will still collect data and use data that is not associated with your account, including to keep our services working smoothly and safely and to support business operations.”.

    Google also warns that your browser may still save your history if you visit a website within a temporary thread. Data could still be collected by the sites you visit and the services those sites use, including Google services like Google Analytics.

    Also: I asked Gemini Notebook to ‘make me a site’ from my notes.

    Industry observers note that for those reasons, you should still be cautious about the information you share even in a temporary thread. But certainly, this option provides greater privacy and protection than a regular AI Mode search.

    Industry observers note that chatGPT, Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot all offer a temporary chat mode that also promises to keep your chats private and unconnected to your account. Claude and Perplexity provide the same feature but call it incognito mode.

    I’m glad to see Google finally offering this option through its AI Mode searches. This marks the second privacy-friendly development in recent days from the search giant. On Tuesday, Google announced that it would be rolling out new settings through which you could opt out of AI model training without losing access to your chat history.

    10 stocks we like better than Salesforce ›.

    The shift toward enterprise automation and artificial intelligence has created a fierce battle between two cloud software titans. Investors choosing between Salesforce (CRM -1.47%) and ServiceNow (NOW -1.42%) must decide which platform offers better value.

    Salesforce dominates the customer relationship management space, helping businesses track every client interaction. ServiceNow specializes in streamlining back-office workflows, from IT support to HR tasks. Both companies are now racing to integrate generative AI into their ecosystems, making this a pivotal comparison for investors seeking growth in tech stocks.

    Salesforce provides cloud-based software that connects sales, marketing, and IT on a single platform to serve over 150,000 companies. It has recently prioritized AI integration through a major partnership with Microsoft (MSFT -2.77%) for "Copilotforce," which combines customer context with AI experiences. The company continues expanding its reach through acquisitions such as Braze (BRZE +0.09%) to deepen engagement. Salesforce serves businesses of all sizes globally, and no single customer accounts for more than 10% of its total revenue.

    Recent findings suggest that in the 12 months ended July 31, 2026, revenue reached approximately $43.9 billion, representing growth of nearly 11.2% over the prior period. The company also generated net income of roughly $9.7 billion, which reflects a net margin of close to 22%. This growth trend has been supported by a steady increase in revenue from $34.9 billion just two years ago. The business focuses on maintaining profitability while scaling its cloud ecosystem and proprietary AI tools.

    As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.3x, which compares total debt to shareholder equity. The current ratio, a measure of how well a tech giant covers short-term debts with short-term assets, is approximately 0.8x. In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, free cash flow was nearly $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    ServiceNow offers an AI platform designed to automate enterprise work across departments including IT, human resources, and finance. The organization focuses on large enterprise clients, ending recent periods with over 600 customers spending more than $5 million annually. It maintains strategic partnerships with Nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) and Accenture (ACN +1.19%) to drive AI-driven workflow integrations for its 8,700 total customers. This strategy targets a growing presence in the public sector and large organizations seeking efficient digital transformation.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached close to $15.4 billion, marking revenue growth of approximately 21.8% over the preceding year. ServiceNow reported net income of nearly $1.4 billion for this period, yielding a net margin of approximately 9.4%. While its net margin is lower than its rival, the tech giant has consistently increased its top line from $9.0 billion two years prior. This expansion reflects robust demand for workflow automation tools across global markets.

    Sources indicate that as of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 0.2x. The current ratio, which measures the ability to cover short-term obligations using liquid assets, is roughly 1.0x, and free cash flow reached nearly $4.6 billion in the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 35.9% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

    Salesforce faces intense competition from established software vendors and AI-native firms entering the customer relationship management space. Integrating large-scale acquisitions like Braze involves execution risks that could disrupt operations if not managed carefully. The company also navigates cybersecurity threats and potential volatility from shifting its pricing models toward consumption-based structures.

    ServiceNow must prove it can continue competing effectively as the AI market evolves rapidly. The company relies on third-party cloud providers and faces regulatory scrutiny related to its growing government contracting business. Additionally, any failure to realize benefits from its aggressive merger and acquisition strategy could impact future growth prospects if integration costs exceed the value gained.

    Salesforce appears more attractively priced on a relative basis, carrying a lower Forward P/E based on future earnings estimates and a lower P/S ratio measuring value against sales over the past twelve months.

    Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.

    ServiceNow's AI business is growing fast, and overall sales are still rising rapidly. The stock plunged after its latest earnings report, as investors worried about slower growth in future contracts and about AI hurting software companies. But management has raised its AI goal twice this year, and the drop leaves the shares well below where they traded before.

    In a recent development, to be fair to Salesforce, it is the cheaper stock and it is buying back a lot of its own shares. Its AI products are also catching on. But its sales are growing more slowly, and part of that growth came from buying another firm. For long-term investors, ServiceNow offers a fast-growing AI business on top of software customers rarely leave, at a lower price after the recent sell-off.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that linux is all about choice.
    • Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.
    • If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that linux is all about choice. From the kernel all the way up to the desktop environment, you get to determine what is used and even how it is used. The staggering number of distributions, desktops, package managers, file managers, and terminal apps provide you with a nearly infinite combination of choices. That choice is and has always been a key aspect of Linux.

    Also: My favorite Linux desktop environment for laptops surprised even me.

    So too is innovation. If there’s one thing that separates Linux from all other operating systems, it’s the willingness to try something different. Linux developers are always pushing the limits of what an operating system is, and this fresh take on the OS is the epitome of that.

    The distribution in question is called Pond. According to the developers, “Pond is an opportunity for us to play with familiar conventions and experiment with new ideas that make a computer more natural and satisfying.”.

    It has been revealed that the developers have achieved something special. Pond takes the standard UI and turns it on its head. Part tiling window manager, part mobile UI, part GNOME, and part something we’ve never before seen, this desktop environment is special. It took me all of five minutes to fall in love with what they’ve created.

    The Pond UI consists of the following:.

    Also: The only 4 Linux email clients I recommend.

    It has been revealed that if you’ve ever considered using a tiling window manager, but thought the lack of a mouse made it seem a bit too complicated, Pond is exactly what you want. Here’s how it works:.

    Pond uses the Niri window manager to arrange windows in columns along an infinite strip from left to right. In multi-monitor setups, each display gets its own strip, so windows never “overflow” from one monitor to the next.

    Also: How to install Arch Linux without losing your mind.

    At the same time, workspaces are dynamic, and there’s always a newly introduced workspace automatically created to the right of the farthest-right window. The combination of the Pond sidebar and Niri’s way of handling windows makes this UI truly original.

    Pond doesn’t have a traditional desktop menu. Instead, you open the launcher (using the Super+Space key combination), type the name of the app you want to install, and hit Enter when the app name appears on both the display and as an icon in the top portion of the sidebar.

    Industry observers note that another thing that sets Pond apart is how you install apps. Yes, you can open a terminal window and install an app using the pacman command, or you can open the launcher, type install, press Enter, and then type the name of the app you want to install. For instance, if you wanted to install LibreOffice, you would type:.

    Once you hit Enter a second time, the installation will begin. Many apps install via Flatpak, but on the off-chance an app must be installed via the pacman package manager, you’ll be prompted to type your user password before the installation begins.

    As I hinted earlier, Pond is based on Arch Linux, which means it’s a rolling-release distribution. One matter that did give me pause was the lack of a GUI enhancement system, which indicates that updates would have to happen in the terminal, like so:.

    I installed the Shelly GUI frontend, which does have an upgrade component. Personally, I would simply open the terminal window, type sudo pacman -Syu, hit Enter, and let the update run in the background. But if a GUI is your jam, Shelly is what you want.

    Also: A super fast distro for anyone ready to move beyond beginner Linux.

    It would be sweet if the developers allowed updating the system from within the launcher, so it didn’t require opening the terminal first. The Pond launcher does allow running system commands from the launcher, which will then open the terminal window and execute the command. For instance, open the terminal, type a command, hit Enter, and then scroll through the list of available commands that can be run.

    Pond ships with kernel 7.3.4-3, so it has outstanding hardware recognition and performance.

    Industry observers note that you should definitely give Pond a try, especially if you’re adventurous and want to experience something completely different. If, on the other hand, different is not in your stream, then Pond will frustrate you to no end.

    Also: Why Nextcloud Office is my new favorite free productivity suite.

    Sources indicate that pond excited me more than any OS has in a very long time; so much so that I could see this becoming my go-to OS, once it reaches stable release. Until then, I will keep Pond installed on a laptop, keep upgrading, and see what happens next.

    Kudos to the Pond OS team for coming up with something truly unique in an already competitive world.

    "Not gonna shut the door on him [Beck], but we're gonna proceed as if Josh is gonna be starting on Sunday," LaFleur remarked.

    Beck, who is a rookie, was thrust into the role of starter after Gardner Minshew went on injured reserve with a torn UCL. The Cardinals' original starter, Jacoby Brissett, was traded to the Baltimore Ravens after being benched for Minshew mid-game the week before.

    Beck was officially ruled as questionable in Friday's injury report.

    Industry observers note that laFleur said in his press conference that the team will monitor how Beck responds to treatment and how he feels on Saturday before making any final decisions. The coach added that this is an issue that Beck has dealt with before, but wasn't able to provide a clear timeline for Beck's return.

    In the meantime, Johnson, who was signed off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad after the Minshew injury, looks poised to be stepping up for Sunday's matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

    The itinerant backup quarterback also has some history with LaFleur: Johnson and LaFleur's careers overlapped in 2021, when both were with the Newly introduced York Jets (LaFleur was an offensive coordinator at the time). LaFleur had high praise for Johnson, noting some of the reasons he's been able to keep his career going this long.

    Industry observers note that "If it is Josh, I've called plays for him before, and had a really great experience calling plays for him," LaFleur said. "He is incredible in the quarterback room, he's incredible for the starters. He's incredible for young quarterbacks, in terms of the way he sees the game, his energy, his positivity, how he keeps it real. He's mature. And he can still sling it. … If that's the route that ends up happening, let's go.".

    Arizona is the 15th NFL franchise that Johnson has been a part of in his career, as the 40-year-old quarterback has bounced between half of the teams in the league. Across 16 seasons, he has only started 11 games in his NFL career.

    Meta Muse booked an Airbnb without permission – and that’s not the worst of it

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (693 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations.
    • According to recent reports, also: Don’t use Muse?
    • According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse said the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Meta’s Muse AI agent has only been around for a few months, but already has a track record of user privacy violations. Even Meta employees are reporting concerning incidents, including the agent taking actions they didn’t ask it to and sharing information they didn’t recognize that appears to belong to other customers.

    According to recent reports, also: Don’t use Muse? Meta’s AI agent can still access your private messages.

    According to a Reuters investigation, Meta employees testing Muse said the agent messaged them about topics they hadn’t asked it about, including career advice, a follow-up on a request for childcare, products they hadn’t purchased, and, crucially, bank account balances they didn’t recognize.

    These incidents “prompted unnerved employees to raise concerns it could be mixing up conversations between different accounts and exposing users’ private data,” Reuters said.

    Reuters remarked “an employee told colleagues his Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: ‘BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2,722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5,899.57.'” In another instance, Muse booked a non-refundable Airbnb for an employee who hadn’t instructed it to.

    Muse notified another employee, who was using the agent on her personal phone, about a message she’d received on Signal, though she remarked she hadn’t given the agent access to the encrypted messaging app.

    Also: Meta Muse is the worst AI agent for privacy – and I’ve tried them all.

    Reuters and the AI Now Institute determined, through testing on an Android phone and a Mac, that Muse used “permissions granted during the bot’s initial setup to pull in the message text, leveraging those authorizations in ways a user might not anticipate.” Because Muse is set up with automatic access to Android push notifications, it didn’t need explicit app access to read messages.

    The tests did not work on an iPhone, suggesting better protections against Muse’s prying.

    Recent findings suggest that similarly, in September, a user reported Muse had shared his address with a Facebook Marketplace buyer before checking with him. The incident was ultimately a misunderstanding between the terms the user thought he’d consented to and how much access he was actually handing over, which exemplifies that Meta and the user may have explicitly different definitions of access, and that Muse can take advantage of that grey area.

    Meta told Reuters these incidents were either isolated or the result of hallucinations, though Reuters could not confirm that.

    Recent findings suggest that these are just the latest in a string of alarming incidents surrounding Muse. In its first month, a cybersecurity professional discovered Muse had a serious zero-day bug that made it hijackable. At least one journalist found the AI sifting through his Apple Messages after he’d explicitly denied those permissions, which Apple then issued stronger privacy protections to address. Banks have also blocked agents over concerns.

    According to recent reports, as a company, Meta doesn’t have a solid history of respecting user privacy. That legacy is partly what informed ZDNET contributor David Gewirtz’s suspicion of the AI assistant when he tested it, though it earned his assigned title of “worst AI agent for privacy” all on its own. The agent asked him for everything from contacts and chats to his logins and passwords, and Meta automatically uses conversations with Muse to train its AI.

    Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac.

    Recent findings suggest that public awareness of the risks of AI agents hit a peak last year with the viral OpenClaw. The predominant advice for using agents has been to take every privacy precaution: Be careful with the data you share and the apps you give it permissions for, and watch what you tell it. But if customers believe they’re doing so by restricting access to certain apps, just for Muse to find a way in anyway, privacy hygiene isn’t enough.

    Also: How to keep your chatbot conversations as private as possible.

    Reuters’ findings may provide an opportunity for Google’s agentic offering, now called Tasks (formerly Spark), which it made free (with usage limits, like Muse) this week.

    #27855. Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1011 w)
    📖 Baca
    AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cnet ↗ Open Full Page

    Why You Shouldn’t Use Meta’s Muse AI Agent for Shopping Next Weekend

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1011 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cnet

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people upcoming tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.
    • Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches.
    • AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It’s been over two months since Meta debuted its Muse AI agent, giving people upcoming tools to automate tasks like handling email replies, booking travel or even shopping for you.

    Muse has been highly controversial, the subject of several security warnings and privacy breaches. Meta’s Muse AI agent quietly builds a profile on you the second you start using it, even if you explicitly tell it not to. That turns Jolly, its supposedly cute and cuddly mascot, into the friendly face of some serious security flaws.

    AI agents are marketed as providing convenience by acting on your behalf. But the trade-off is privacy and control. You’re handing over your personal information to a black box with little visibility into how it’s used. Multiple incidents are fueling a conversation about the dangers of agentic AI and whether they require higher security standards before being granted access to user data.

    That’s especially the case when it comes to handing over sensitive financial information. If you give an AI access to your digital wallets to shop for you, the risk extends beyond an authorized purchase. You could be exposing your bank accounts to a potential security breach or data exposure, with little recourse to fix it. If you were considering letting Muse make decisions and transactions with your money ahead of Black Friday and Cyber Monday, you should know it’s still raising red flags as a shopping companion.

    In a recent development, given Meta’s track record of privacy fines, data sharing and security problems, it’s worth proceeding with caution. A few months ago, a lifestyle blogger reported that the social media platform’s AI asked intrusive questions about her kids and pieced together private information about her life from her posts. Meta’s controversial smart glasses have received pushback on multiple fronts — from its facial recognition software to the way it captures and stores data.

    Sources indicate that despite the risk, Muse has remained popular and now faces competition from Anthropic’s newly released Claude Duet, another AI business agent. Meta is also releasing a $300 portable device, Charm, in a virtual-toy style that will work with Muse.

    A representative for Meta has not responded to CNET’s request for comment.

    Muse asks for the keys to your digital life: passwords, full disk access, emails, calendar invites, contacts, Notes and WhatsApp chats. Meta also feeds your conversations into its AI training pipeline by default, leaving it on you to dig through the settings and opt out.

    In a recent development, within weeks of launch earlier this fall, a security researcher demonstrated that the assistant could be hijacked via a zero-day exploit that Meta’s own documentation acknowledged was easy to trigger. Then, an investigative journalist discovered Muse digging through his private Apple Messages without permission. Meta disputed the claim, but Apple took it seriously enough to roll out an emergency enhancement to MacOS privacy controls.

    More recently, Meta employees themselves have flagged instances where Muse may have accessed encrypted messages from apps such as Signal or information from other Muse users, which Meta has chalked up to “isolated incidents” and that permission to access apps and information from notifications has to be explicitly granted in a statement to news outlets.

    If the previous incidents weren’t enough to give you pause, there’s also a widely publicized case in which Muse mistakenly shared the home address of a Toronto tech reviewer, Matt Robb, with a potential buyer on Facebook Marketplace. Muse invited the stranger to Robb’s home without his explicit consent or knowledge, then later apologized for doing so, as detailed in a Threads post. Robb hadn’t realized that he had inadvertently granted Muse blanket permission to automatically reply to Marketplace inquiries using the details he provided, including his address.

    Before facing a potential security nightmare, here are a few other things to know about Muse.

    Muse uploads iOS or Mac data even when you tell it not to: Meta’s Muse appears to blatantly ignore user permissions, according to a September report by AppleInsider. In one case, the AI agent synced roughly 187,000 lines of a user’s Apple Messages without their consent, even though “Full Disk Access” was turned off. The report demonstrates that Muse pinged a user’s messages database thousands of times despite disk access being disabled. Muse then successfully harvested texts from the user’s Mac — not from Meta’s Messenger, but from Apple Messages. Even people who refuse to use Muse may have their data collected by the AI if they text someone who does have it installed.

    Sources indicate that muse could hand over data to human callers: Before Meta debuted the ability for its Muse to make outbound business calls on your behalf, internal Meta documents revealed that the firm planned to rely on human contractors at call centers to help make reservations and appointments. That means not only would the software have access to all your private data, but a total stranger might also be managing your personal commitments — all without your knowledge. The human concierge feature appears to have been rolled back for now, according to Reuters.

    It has been revealed that muse has the most robust data collection: In September, the VPN tech giant Surfshark mentioned it found that Meta Muse is collecting — or attempting to collect — 31 out of 35 types of data, putting it far ahead of other popular chatbots like Gemini, ChatGPT and DeepSeek. Muse also collects highly sensitive personal information like location data, sexual orientation, genetic information or biometric data. Muse (along with Meta AI and Gemini) also reserves the right to use collected audio data for other purposes, such as analytics or product personalization. Surfshark released a full dataset of what it uncovered.

    Meta has tried hard with Muse to make the AI agent seem cute and approachable, but when it comes to your money and giving Muse access to it, it’s best to be very cautious for the time being.

    According to recent reports, want to share your experience with Meta’s Muse or other AI agents? Email us at editors@cnet.com.

    Signal to restrict screenshots over AI agent concerns – again

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Zdnet

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set upcoming limits on screenshots.
    • Whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers.
    • Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that privacy concerns around AI agents have prompted encrypted messaging app Signal to set upcoming limits on screenshots. The manufacturer will prevent screenshotting in its iOS 27 app and “when AI assistants attempt to capture screen data on Android,” Signal President Meredith Whittaker wrote in a blog post Friday.

    Whittaker noted that Google and Apple’s agentic features, including Gemini Intelligence and Siri AI’s Onscreen Awareness, compromise the privacy missions of third-party developers. These features observe what’s on a user’s screen as context for completing requests.

    Also: My 5 favorite Siri AI ‘onscreen awareness’ tricks – and why.

    According to recent reports, “Your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” Whittaker noted. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

    Signal also blocked screenshots last year in response to Microsoft’s controversial Recall AI feature, which could capture screenshots of Signal chats on devices running Windows 11.

    Signal’s move is another reminder of how Massive Tech’s AI strategy trickles downstream. As AI features have moved from services external to the OS (like chatbots from OpenAI or Anthropic) to further inside of it, third-party apps have to adapt to conditions that undermine their hard-won privacy infrastructure.

    Also: How I use Meta Muse safely to stretch my AI budget – and what I never let it do.

    Recent findings suggest that just last week, researchers at Google DeepMind used AI agents to formally verify Signal’s code, building on Signal’s own work to essentially prove the app’s encryption works. That’s a high bar for a security guarantee within the app, but it becomes meaningless if an agent can simply grab messages off a screen.

    Samsung is reportedly working on its own agent, Galaxy Claw, and Apple is developing a rival for Claude and ChatGPT as well.

    Whittaker noted Signal’s screenshot restriction isn’t perfect, saying that AI agents can still access app data through other means, “such as retrieving content already present on a user’s device via the filesystem.” Earlier this week, a Reuters investigation supported by Signal and the AI Now Institute found that Meta’s Muse AI agent was using permissions from its initial setup in unexpected ways to access apps and data that a user had not explicitly connected it to.

    Signal said its protections don’t presently work on MacOS.

    Sources indicate that “It is a serious problem that Signal – and application developers beyond – lack robust tools to prevent AI agents from undermining application-level privacy,” she added. “Even where we are able to detect and block AI data access, Google, Apple, Microsoft, and others do not provide ways for developers to easily restrict such AI data access without making drastic compromises to the core user experience.”.

    If you’d still like to take screenshots, you can simply disable the setting, though Signal’s announcement strongly advised against it.

    “Doing so will potentially expose your (and your contacts’) Signal content to these AI agents, and break our privacy guarantees,” Whittaker mentioned.

    If you're here looking for lower mortgage interest rates, today is definitely not your day.

    The average interest rate on a 30-year, fixed-rate mortgage jumped to 7.38% APR, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. This is 25 basis points higher than yesterday and 12 basis points higher than a week ago. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.).

    Keep in mind that mortgage rates are always on the move, and that if you're tracking rates day-to-day, you're going to see a lot of volatility. Zooming out and looking at the bigger picture — like a graph showing at least a month's worth of rate data — can help you see the overall trend.

    Here are the average APRs we're seeing today, as well as movement over the past month for context:.

    » Take the next step: Compare mortgage rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    Mortgage rates are constantly changing, since a major part of how rates are set depends on reactions to upcoming inflation reports, job numbers, Fed meetings, global news ... you name it. For example, even tiny changes in the bond market can shift mortgage pricing.

    In a recent development, on Friday, the Bureau of Labor Statistics released the Producer Price Index for October, which tracks the change in prices that U.S. producers are able to get for their products. This is one way to measure inflation on the market end, rather than the consumer end.

    The results were mixed. While prices didn’t rise quite as high as economists anticipated month-over-month (0.3% vs. 0.4%), year-over-year price growth did reach 6.5% — the largest increase in four years. This points to even higher costs for consumers coming in the near future.

    Recent findings suggest that investors are convinced that the Federal Reserve will raise overnight borrowing rates again in December to pull inflation down. And higher overnight borrowing rates — called the federal funds rate, which is what banks pay to fund products like mortgages — usually lead to higher mortgage rates.

    » MORE: How the Federal Reserve affects mortgage rates.

    Refinancing might make sense if today’s rates are at least 0.5 to 0.75 of a percentage point lower than your current rate (and if you proposal to stay in your home long enough to break even on closing costs).

    With rates where they are right now, you may want to start considering a refi if your current rate is around 7.88% or higher — but there aren’t many people for whom that’s true.

    Also consider your goals: Are you trying to lower your monthly payment, shorten your loan term or turn home equity into cash? For example, you might be more comfortable with paying a higher rate for a cash-out refinance than you would for a rate-and-term refinance, so long as the overall costs are lower than if you kept your original mortgage and added a HELOC or home equity loan.

    If you're looking for a lower rate, use NerdWallet's refinance calculator to estimate savings and understand how long it would take to break even on the costs of refinancing.

    » Time to refi? Compare refinance rates from NerdWallet’s top lenders.

    There is no universal “right” time to start shopping — what matters is whether you can comfortably afford a mortgage now at today’s rates.

    According to recent reports, if the answer is yes, don’t get too hung up on whether you could be missing out on lower rates later; you can refinance down the road. Focus on getting preapproved, comparing lender offers, and understanding what monthly payment works for your budget.

    According to recent reports, nerdWallet’s affordability calculator can help you estimate your potential monthly payment. If a new home isn’t in the cards right now, there are still things you can do to strengthen your buyer profile. Take this time to pay down existing debts and build your down payment savings. Not only will this free up more cash flow for a future mortgage payment, it can also get you a better interest rate when you’re ready to buy.

    » Is now a good time to buy? See NerdWallet’s analysis.

    According to recent reports, if you already have a quote you’re happy with, you should consider locking your mortgage rate, especially if your lender offers a float-down option. A float-down lets you take advantage of a better rate if the market drops during your lock period.

    Rate locks protect you from increases while your loan is processed, and with the market forever bouncing around, that peace of mind can be worth it.

    • Sources indicate that all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Google Home is replacing Nest and bringing latest devices.

    If you’re a Nest smart home user, a major change is coming in early 2027 that will affect how you manage your smart home. Google has officially confirmed to CNET via email that both the Nest app and Google Assistant are being sunset, and current users will lose access to both next year.

    Sources indicate that all Nest devices will lose Nest app support in favor of the Google Home app, and the Nest app will be retired on Jan. 25, 2027. Google Assistant will be removed from home devices on Aug. 2, 2027, with all support moving to the Gemini for Home voice assistant.

    In a recent development, the change is part of Google’s effort to consolidate its various apps and devices into a single app and voice experience. In a statement sent to CNET, Google confirmed that “every device supported today works with these updated experiences.”.

    Nest Thermostats should all seamlessly port over to Google Home.

    Google has confirmed that Google Home will support all your Nest devices, including thermostats, cameras, doorbells, smoke detectors and locks. Existing schedules and settings should transfer over automatically, which is often a hassle when you switch between apps and devices. You should also be able to pair your Nest devices with any Works with Google Home and Matter smart home devices, as well as Google Home speakers and smart displays and TV streamers, all with the same app.

    As part of the switchover, you should be able to access Nest devices on various platforms outside of the mobile app. It’ll support iOS and Android widgets, the Home Panel on Android, smart displays, speakers and the Google Home web page. That includes being able to check live camera views, adjust your thermostat and lock your front door, right from a TV or smartwatch.

    Google Assistant may be leaving, but Google is releasing newer, more powerful devices.

    In a recent development, google notes that, in addition to devices automatically appearing in the Favorites tab in the Google Home app, you should be able to see camera views faster and access the most-used controls the moment you open the app. Part of the goal is to give people the latest security protections and cyber defenses, as well as Google Account security, privacy controls and threat protections –- all things that seem extra relevant these days as major companies across the US seem to be experiencing outages.

    However, to continue controlling and receiving notifications from your Nest devices remotely, you will need to switch to the Google Home app or home.google.com if you prefer to control them via a web browser.

    You can change Google voice assistant voices, but not the wake words.

    On Aug. 2, 2027, Gemini for Home voice assistant will fully replace Google Assistant on speakers and smart displays. The switch to Gemini makes a lot of sense if you’ve used Google Assistant at all. Assistant is very much an older voice assistant, lacking the smarter follow-ups and natural-language capabilities that make Gemini more useful.With Gemini, you should get answers to more complex questions, and you can speak more naturally without barking commands, letting it handle conversation context and remember multiple interactions.

    Getting ready for Google Home is easy, though Google has an entire Nest App Transition Support Hub if you need step-by-step instructions to walk you through everything that’s needed.

    For most people, it should be a simple matter of downloading the Google Home app. Naturally, a Google Account is required, but as mentioned, your Nest devices, including the cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app starting on Jan. 25, 2027.

    Gemini’s Google Home integrations are useful, but command options can include some risks.

    The other thing you may have to do is download any custom video clips you’ve created on home.nest.com. Manually saved clips won’t transfer to the Google Home app along with your video history. To make sure these are backed up, you’ll want to visit home.nest.com before Jan. 25, 2027, and use the Download All button to save clips you want to keep.

    The final deadline to migrate your Nest account to a Google account before the firm starts data deletions March 25, 2027.

    Google states Nest devices, including cameras and video history, will automatically transfer from the Nest app to the Google Home app. Nest Aware (1st Gen) subscriptions should also automatically switch to Google Home Premium so that coverage continues without interruption. Google Home Premium is replacing Nest Aware (1st Gen), and users will receive an email closer to the transfer date detailing your subscription information.

    Google’s smart displays should all work perfectly with the various Nest devices.

    Gemini for Home is already available in many countries and languages. Google unveiled earlier that it’s expanding to more regions over the coming months. Users in a supported region can upgrade to Gemini Home right now.

    On your phone, open the latest version of the Google Home app, tap your profile icon in the top right to open Home Settings, then tap “Get Started” on the “Set up Gemini for Home” banner. On your computer, just visit home.google.com/gemini.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that this is not your parents’ Google home page. In its push to get more users to adopt its AI tools, the search engine giant is rolling out a raft of fresh features worldwide.

    In a recent development, the new elements include three new buttons below the search bar at Google.com: Create images, Ask about files and Brainstorm. The Google Search button is gone, but the I’m Feeling Lucky button remains.

    In a recent development, the buttons are available when using Google on a desktop but not on mobile. I was able to see the new buttons when signed in to my Google account.

    When signed out, I was only able to see the typical home page, with the only AI button being AI Mode, which has been there since May 2025.

    Sources indicate that clicking on the “Create images” button opens up a newly introduced page where you can create an AI-generated image using Google’s Nano Banana. It’s the same image-generation tool you can use on other Google platforms such as the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and AI Mode in Search.

    Clicking “Ask about files” allows for several options. You can have the AI analyze a document and rewrite it, simply have it answer questions or ask it to perform tasks such as “polish my resume” or “draft an email with action items.”.

    The “Brainstorm” button prompts you to “describe your goal,” such as making a to-do list, learning how to code or finding a table at a restaurant.

    Another new feature, as confirmed by Google Search Product VP Robby Stein on X, is a collapsible sidebar on the left side of the home page, which highlights your recent AI search threads and offers the ability to create a new one:.

    Stein mentioned the upcoming sidebar will help consumers go back to where they left off.

    “People are coming to Search with more questions that aren’t just one and done — and in testing, this sidebar made a massive difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web,” Stein posted.

    I didn’t see the collapsible sidebar during my testing of the home page.

    In a recent development, google will use your AI searches — whether they are questions, tasks, uploaded files or image generation — to train its AI models, but you can tell Google you’re opting out. CNET has an overview of how to tell chatbots not to use your data. Still, for Google specifically, you can go to Data and Privacy > My Activity > Other activity > Gemini Apps Activity to turn off AI training.

    Sources indicate that google has integrated its Gemini AI models throughout its various platforms — Search, Gmail, Docs, Pixel phones and third-party apps such as Adobe, Shopify, OpenTable and Instacart. This past week, Google announced several other latest AI features — integrations with stores such as Albertsons, Safeway and Target to complete orders and connect to apps such as Peloton and Adobe.

    Over the summer, Google’s Gemini app topped 1 billion people in what CEO Sundar Pichai called the company’s “fastest growing product ever.”.

    According to recent reports, but Google’s rush to force-feed AI into its products has met with plenty of pushback. The Upcoming York City, Los Angeles and Chicago school districts said they might choose different search engines because Google said it will not remove AI from search tools used by students, The New York Times reported.

    Google noted search and the Gemini app will be turned off for schools unless school administrators want them. But Google said there will not be a chatbot-free version of search available for schools. So schools declining AI will not be able to search using Google at all.

    Google’s AI Overviews, which appear at the top of many search page results, have also been blamed for a steep drop in web traffic to content publishers. AI Overviews summarize user search queries and replace the long list of blue hyperlinks that once appeared across search pages. So instead of clicking on those links to get more information, giving publishers valuable clicks, a user can simply get their query response by reading the AI Overview.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.
    • Industry observers note that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty?
    • Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A Redditor recently shared that they were struggling to decide which financial steps to take first after a job loss.

    Industry observers note that should they withdraw money from retirement savings to have more cash on hand — but pay an early withdrawal penalty? Or is it better to rely on the severance payout to handle expenses?

    Many users responded with good ideas: File for unemployment, try to avoid tapping into retirement savings, and cut expenses as much as possible.

    For more ideas, I asked three financial experts how to manage money in the immediate aftermath of job loss.

    While it’s tempting to make quick decisions about tapping into a retirement fund or selling a house, it’s better to wait on any significant moves, says Parker Wine, retirement planning advisor at the financial firm Daniel A. White & Associates in Lewes, Delaware.

    According to recent reports, that’s because you need time to digest the situation and weigh the pros and cons of different options, he notes. “People can get impulsive and panic, and it’s usually a bad thing to make decisions when you’re panicking,” he says.

    Take your time, get second opinions and think through all of your options first, Wine suggests.

    If you’re fortunate enough to receive a severance package, wait to sign it until you’ve reviewed it carefully and understand all of the details, claims John Rafferty, partner and investment advisor representative at Solomon Financial in Carmel, Indiana.

    For example, make sure you know about your health insurance options, such as whether you’ll receive insurance through COBRA or need to take out a latest policy in the health insurance marketplace.

    Filing for unemployment and checking into any other available workplace benefits — such as help with your new job search — is also an crucial part of understanding what support to expect in the weeks and months ahead, Rafferty adds.

    Creating a bare-bones budget stripped of “extras” like restaurant meals or travel can help the severance payment last as long as possible, Rafferty indicates.

    “Now that you don’t have income coming in, ask yourself, ‘How much can I spend and where?’”.

    You might be able to cut back on entertainment costs, coffee runs and clothing purchases, for example.

    It has been revealed that at the same time, it’s notable to prioritize the essentials like mortgage payments, rent, utilities and food. Rafferty recommends calling your mortgage company, utilities provider and any other lenders to ask if they have a hardship program for those experiencing financial challenges.

    Opting in could give you more time to pay your bills or temporarily lower payments.

    It’s hard to stick to a budget that eliminates all entertainment, so Rafferty suggests finding enjoyable activities that come with a low price tag. Hiking, discovering a fresh park and participating in free community events are all ways to enjoy downtime on a budget.

    According to recent reports, “Having that release is mentally a substantial thing so you can stay prepared for the job search,” he says. “Otherwise, it’s easy to get down and feel negative, and we need things to help us feel positive.”.

    Similarly, connecting with friends and family during this time is crucial, notes Laura Adams, accredited financial counselor and financial coach in Wilmington, North Carolina.

    In a recent development, people often feel a sense of shame or embarrassment after job loss, and Adams encourages people to talk about their feelings and ask for help if needed. “Financial shame can cause us to make emotional rather than confident financial decisions,” she indicates.

    In a recent development, starting some kind of side hustle to bring in extra cash can also help bridge the gap between the job loss and your next job, Wine says. Substitute teaching, working at a local public golf course and driving for a rideshare service are all options he’s seen people try.

    Doing something new also helps stave off boredom while unemployed, but he cautions that you’ll still owe taxes on any side income you bring in, so proposal accordingly.

    Recent findings suggest that all three financial experts also emphasized that a job loss is easier to handle with an emergency savings fund you can turn to, and suggested building one up — ideally three to six months’ worth of expenses. But starting small helps, too — while employed, if possible.

    In a recent development, the Redditor who posted the question mentioned that, like many Americans, they lacked emergency savings. This added urgency to the question of what to prioritize.

    Reddit is an online forum where users share their thoughts in “threads” on various topics. The popular site includes plenty of discussion on financial subjects like how to deal with job loss, so we sifted through Reddit forums to get a pulse check. People post anonymously, so we cannot confirm their individual experiences or circumstances.

    With Mortgage Rates Rising, Should You Hibernate Until Spring?

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.
    • The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov.
    • A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Mortgage rates are back up this week, wiping out modest relief from a monthlong drop that began in mid-October.

    The average rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage shot up 29 basis points to 7.28% APR in the week ending Nov. 19, according to rates provided to NerdWallet by Zillow. (A basis point is one one-hundredth of a percentage point.) We calculate our weekly average using daily APRs recorded over the past five business days.

    A mortgage is a big ol’ loan, so when rates go up, those fractions of a percentage point add up fast. Say you’re borrowing $400,000 on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage. Compared with last week, your monthly principal and interest payment would be about $78 higher today.

    Sources indicate that one bad week doesn't make a trend, but a jump like this can make putting your house hunt on hold until spring feel like a safer bet. So … is it?

    Before deciding whether to buy a house now or wait, it helps to know what's pushing mortgage rates higher.

    Right now, mortgage rates are still feeling the aftershocks from two major inflation reports last week. First, the Consumer Price Index (CPI) revealed consumer prices rose more than expected in October. Then, the Producer Price Index (PPI) showed wholesale inflation climbed 6.5% over the past year — its biggest annual increase in nearly four years.

    According to recent reports, while CPI reveals how prices have changed, PPI can offer clues about what's coming next. Faced with higher costs, businesses may raise their own prices to compensate, keeping inflation elevated. Federal Reserve policymakers aren't expecting much relief anytime soon, either. According to meeting minutes released Nov. 18, they expect inflation to remain elevated above their 2% target for a while.

    To cool rising prices, the Fed can raise the federal funds rate, which is the benchmark interest rate banks charge each other for overnight loans. The Fed doesn't set mortgage rates, but lenders anticipate its decisions, so mortgage rates often move before the Fed acts. A rate hike is widely expected at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting.

    According to recent reports, even after a Fed rate hike, there’s no telling how rapidly inflation will cool — or whether mortgage rates will follow. (Inflation is just one of many forces that affect mortgage rates, after all.) So if you do wait until spring to buy a house, don't do it just because you're betting on a cheaper mortgage.

    If you're not in a rush to move, winter can be a good time to regroup. Fewer homes typically go up for sale from November through February, so waiting until spring could give you more options.

    According to recent reports, but new data from the National Association of Realtors suggests this year's slowdown goes beyond the usual seasonal lull. High mortgage rates and home prices are making it tough for many buyers to make the numbers work. For some buyers, waiting isn't a strategy — it's the only option.

    Industry observers note that pending home sales, a measure of homes under contract, fell 16.7% in October compared with a year earlier, NAR reports. All four U.S. regions saw declines. At this rate, NAR chief economist Lawrence Yun warned that annual home sales could fall to their lowest level since the mid-1990s.

    “Either sizable housing demand is building in the background, or the dream of homeownership is increasingly out of reach for many Americans,” Yun said in a news release.

    Recent findings suggest that whether you're waiting by choice or necessity, you can use the time to strengthen your finances. Paying down debt, strengthening your credit score or saving for a bigger down payment could help you qualify for a better mortgage deal.

    Every little bit helps when today’s mortgage rates are this high.

    Mortgage preapprovals typically expire after 60 to 90 days. If you're already preapproved, why not keep an eye on listings this winter? (Hey, I’m an optimist. All it takes is one house.).

    Sources indicate that think like a seller for a second. If you're listing your house in the dead of winter, you're probably not doing it just for fun. You might have a deadline, and you’re probably more willing to negotiate. In the winter, buyers have less competition — and more room to negotiate a lower price, closing cost credits or repairs. Those savings on the sticker price might help offset today's higher borrowing costs.

    According to recent reports, spring typically brings more homes for sale, but it also brings more buyers competing for them. And if mortgage rates end up dropping this spring, you won't be the only one coming out of hibernation.
