    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nerdwallet ↗ Open Full Page

    This Oceanfront Hilton Resort in Florida Is Great for Groups

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1476 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort.
    • The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R.
    • According to recent reports, room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that hilton is making a big play in South Florida with its Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort. The massive 1,000-room property — which underwent an $80 million renovation before opening under the Signia Hilton brand in May 2026 — sits on the beach in Hollywood, Florida, just outside of Fort Lauderdale.

    The resort caters primarily to business and group travelers (it’s attached to a massive events space), but it’s also a strong option for vacationers looking for some R&R. The main downside: The location isn’t great if your trip primarily revolves around off-property excursions, dining and nightlife.

    According to recent reports, room rates typically run $300 to $600 a night, depending on the season, but you can also use Hilton Honors benefits to make your stay more affordable. There’s also a resort fee of $59 per night — but Hilton waives that when you book using Hilton points.

    Industry observers note that hilton covered the cost of my stay for two nights, but the opinions in this review are my own. Here’s what guests can expect at this oceanfront resort.

    Since the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort is part of Hilton Honors, there are several ways to book a stay there.

    If you’re using Hilton points, expect to pay 70,000 to 80,000 points a night when standard rooms are available. Hilton elite status — a benefit you can earn by holding any Hilton Honors credit card — gets you the fifth-night-free perk, where you stay for at least five nights but pay for four when booking with points.

    For example, if you were to stay five nights at 80,000 points a night, you’d pay 320,000 points total, bringing down your average nightly rate to 64,000 points.

    You can also book using Hilton’s generous free night certificates, which can be used at almost any property in the portfolio. If you hold the Hilton Honors American Express Aspire Card, you automatically get a certificate each year. It’s also possible to earn certificates through reaching spending thresholds on the card and on the Hilton Honors American Express Surpass® Card. Terms apply.

    Make sure to check the cash rate against the points rate to make sure you’re getting good value from your redemption. NerdWallet values Hilton points at 0.4 cent apiece.

    According to recent reports, for cash bookings of two nights or more, you might consider using The Hotel Collection via American Express’ travel portal for eligible cardholders. Eligible bookings come with benefits like a $100 property credit and other amenities subject to availability, including a room upgrade, early check-in and late checkout.

    Keep in mind that third-party bookings typically don’t earn Hilton points or count toward elite status qualification.

    It’s hard to miss the Signia by Hilton Diplomat Beach Resort, with its signature H-shaped facade and sleek white-and-glass exterior.

    Stepping into the hotel, I was immediately struck by the lush greenery filling the entrance and indoor courtyard. The grand lobby has soaring glass ceilings, giving the space a greenhouse feel, although the strong air conditioning keeps you cool.

    Despite its massive size, it doesn’t have a sprawling layout, which I appreciated. Everything is close together, and you can walk from the check-in counter to any of the indoor restaurants in under a minute.

    In a recent development, I stayed in an oceanfront suite with a balcony, which was spacious and had a fun beachy vibe. To get to the rooms, you’ll need to use either the north or south tower elevator banks.

    In the living room, there was a large sitting area featuring a TV, a couch, an accent chair and a four-person high-top table.

    Although I didn’t spend too much time on the balcony — the October balminess was a bit too much for me — I enjoyed stepping out each morning to admire the view.

    The bedroom had a king bed with extremely comfortable bedding and an oversized chair that was a great spot to relax and read a book by the window.

    The bathroom was spacious, featuring a shower and a separate tub (something every room has).

    Even the standard room I toured felt roomy. I liked that it shared similar elements with the suite, including the oversized lounge chair.

    This is what you’d normally get when booking a room at the cheapest points price.

    There are several dining venues on the property, ranging from a grab-and-go cafe to a high-end steakhouse. It is a luxury resort, so expect the prices to reflect that.

    For breakfast, you can head to Palmea Kitchen, which is also open for lunch. I had the breakfast buffet, which offered a nice spread of classics, from hot food items and pastries to cold cuts and smoked salmon.

    If you don’t have time for a sit-down breakfast, you can head next door to The Press, which offers made-to-order and grab-and-go food options throughout the day. You can also get smoothies, juices, snacks, pastries and other sweet treats.

    The Canteen is another grab-and-go option that also sells snacks, drinks, souvenirs and sundries, similar to a convenience store.

    Sources indicate that for lunch and dinner, try Solara. It doesn’t have a traditional restaurant feel, as it’s mostly an indoor-outdoor bar space. One side connects to the lobby, while the other side faces the Solara adults-only pool.

    It serves a lunch menu, as well as a substantial bar food menu that’s available late into the night.

    You can also eat at Playa Beach Bar & Grill, a beachside restaurant serving Latin-inspired cuisine. I enjoyed spending a lazy lunch there and watching the waves crash onto the shore.

    It has been revealed that for a fancy sit-down dinner, go to Diplomat Prime, the property’s steakhouse. We had a group dinner at the restaurant, and the meats were, of course, the highlight. But don’t sleep on the seafood, which was also delicious.

    One of the best parts of the Dip, as it’s affectionately known, is its location right on the beach. Guests can access the stretch of beach directly adjacent to the property. But it’s not a private beach, so you might encounter crowds.

    I didn’t spend any time on the beach itself — it was extremely windy while I was there — but the hotel’s resort fee includes amenities like a beach lounge (umbrella not included), a daily one-hour kayak or paddleboard rental, and beachfront yoga classes.

    If you don’t want to get sand everywhere, you can head to one of the three pool options: the adults-only Solara pool, the family-friendly lagoon pool and the Verandah Social Club for those 21 and older (requires paid access).

    The family-friendly lagoon spans the length of the property and runs beneath the Solara pool. It also has its own hot tub.

    I spent an afternoon in a cabana at the Verandah Social Club, which has some smaller plunge pools and a hot tub.

    I appreciated the attentive service from the staff there, who constantly checked on whether guests needed anything.

    If you’re looking for other ways to stay active, head to the two-story fitness center, featuring a variety of equipment like free weights, exercise bikes, a rowing machine and treadmills.

    According to recent reports, next door, you’ll find the spa and wellness center. I had a relaxing massage that incorporated hot stones and aromatherapy.

    The locker rooms come with a sauna and steam room, although I wished there were more amenities like a hot tub and cold plunge.

    One of the resort fee inclusions is complimentary high-intensity interval training workout classes at the gym across the street. I signed up for an early morning class. The instructor was friendly, and it was a great way to start my day.

    Other amenities include a complimentary one-hour e-bike rental each day, as well as a kids’ club with various activities (but drop-off fees apply).

    I had a fantastic stay at this resort, but I’d recommend it for a specific traveler.

    If you’re planning to stay on-property your entire trip, it’s a great option. That’s probably why it’s such a popular convention hotel, since everything you need is easily accessible.

    I loved the hotel’s design, including the jungle-like atmosphere in the lobby, and I found the dining options to be tasty, albeit pricey.

    But if your trip revolves around visiting Miami attractions, you’ll likely want to stay closer to the action.

    Take-Two Interactive vs. Anthropic: Which Market-Moving Stock Is the Better Buy?

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (657 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Take-Two Interactive (TTWO +0.65%) and Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) are arguably the two stocks that generated the most excitement this week.
    • Anthropic launched its IPO this week, as its Claude artificial intelligence (AI) assistant has generated investor excitement and driven massive revenue growth.
    • Despite that anticipation and the likely boost to Take-Two stock, I believe Anthropic is the better buy, and here's why.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Will Healy – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:33PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Anthropic ›.

    Take-Two Interactive (TTWO +0.65%) and Anthropic (ANT -8.50%) are arguably the two stocks that generated the most excitement this week.

    Anthropic launched its IPO this week, as its Claude artificial intelligence (AI) assistant has generated investor excitement and driven massive revenue growth. That may have been overshadowed by gamers who have awaited Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), possibly since Take-Two released GTA 5 in 2013.

    Despite that anticipation and the likely boost to Take-Two stock, I believe Anthropic is the better buy, and here's why.

    Admittedly, Take-Two might be a more obvious choice since the anticipation for GTA 6 likely predates Anthropic's 2021 founding.

    According to recent reports, with that waiting game now over, Take-Two subsidiary Rockstar Games revealed that it sold 32.5 million copies of the game on day one, generating $3.79 billion in revenue. That is huge considering that the firm reported $3 billion in the first six months of fiscal 2027 (ended Sept. 30). That was game-changing, figuratively and literally, for Take-Two stock, which also reported an 8% year-over-year revenue decline during the same period.

    Furthermore, net losses have left it without a price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio. Still, according to analysts, this sales boost puts Take-Two on track for an estimated 27% yearly revenue gain in fiscal 2027 and a return to profitability. That recovery could make investors more willing to pay its 30 forward P/E ratio.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Unfortunately, game releases are one-off events, and such temporary sales bumps tend to run their course promptly. Consequently, analysts believe the entertainment stock's revenue growth will slow to 6% in fiscal 2028, making the release unlikely to change the company's long-term value proposition.

    Recent findings suggest that in contrast, Anthropic's gains are on track to be more than one-time. Companies from nearly all sectors of the economy are scrambling to incorporate AI into their businesses. This has greatly benefited Claude, which has stood toe-to-toe with the competition from OpenAI's ChatGPT and Alphabet's (GOOGL -2.70%) (GOOG -2.59%) Google Gemini.

    Industry observers note that its financials confirm its fast-growing popularity. The $33 billion it generated in the first nine months of 2026 far exceeded the $2.5 billion it reported during the same period in 2025.

    Moreover, although it lost $104 billion during the first three quarters of 2026, $94 billion of that loss resulted from changes in the fair value of convertible notes. The operating losses were less than $1.3 billion of that total loss, suggesting it could turn an operating profit in the foreseeable future.

    Additionally, even after giving back most of its IPO pop, its price-to-sales (P/S) ratio is around 45, far more than Take-Two's sales multiple of 6.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    For next year, analysts estimate 135% revenue growth. At current prices, that would likely reduce its sales multiple over time, potentially pushing Anthropic stock higher.

    Between Take-Two and Anthropic, I recommend the latter.

    Indeed, the GTA 6 release should put Take-Two on a firmer financial footing. Unfortunately, that sales bump is likely to be temporary, suggesting it cannot rely on one fresh game release to improve Take-Two's long-term value proposition.

    According to recent reports, in contrast, Anthropic has benefited from tremendous AI demand, so much so that it will likely report triple-digit revenue growth for the foreseeable future. That probably means that even with an elevated valuation, it should deliver higher returns to investors over time.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) plunged 14.01% on Friday, November 20, closing at $125.53 as Wall Street's sell-off intensified.
    • According to recent reports, the decline extends a brutal stretch for Nvidia, which has reportedly shed approximately $2.5 trillion in market value from its recent peak despite delivering strong quarterly earnings earlier this week.
    • The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) plunged 3.82% to 6,902, breaking below the psychologically important 7,000 level.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By RJ Fulton – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:35PM EST.

    According to recent reports, nvidia (NVDA -14.01%) plunged 14.01% on Friday, November 20, closing at $125.53 as Wall Street's sell-off intensified. Reports of a Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) accounting investigation added to mounting concerns surrounding the company's regulatory exposure, while growing skepticism over elevated AI valuations continued to weigh on the broader semiconductor industry.

    According to recent reports, the decline extends a brutal stretch for Nvidia, which has reportedly shed approximately $2.5 trillion in market value from its recent peak despite delivering strong quarterly earnings earlier this week. Trading volume surged to 607.8 million shares, approximately 262% above its three-month daily average of 167.9 million, reflecting the intensity of the selling pressure.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    The S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) plunged 3.82% to 6,902, breaking below the psychologically important 7,000 level. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) tumbled 5.13% to 22,654 as investors continued to retreat from high-growth technology stocks.

    Selling pressure was particularly severe across the semiconductor industry. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD -13.25%) plunged 13.26% to $424.32, while Broadcom (AVGO -12.19%) fell 12.12% to $304.65. The widespread losses suggest investors are reassessing the valuations and near-term outlook for AI-related companies, even as demand for advanced computing infrastructure remains strong.

    Industry observers note that nvidia's latest sell-off highlights a growing disconnect between the manufacturer's financial performance and investor expectations. Despite reporting exceptional quarterly revenue growth and raising its outlook, shares have continued to decline alongside the broader semiconductor industry. With fresh SEC scrutiny of Nvidia's accounting practices and tightening U.S. semiconductor export restrictions adding to uncertainty, investors are increasingly questioning whether the company's exceptional growth can justify its valuation amid deteriorating market conditions.

    Looking ahead, the central question is whether Nvidia can sustain its growth and profitability as major technology companies face increasing pressure to demonstrate returns on their AI investments. A slowdown in data center spending, tighter export restrictions, or additional regulatory developments could force analysts to reassess Nvidia's earnings projections for 2027.

    For investors considering buying the dip, the distinction between a falling stock price and an improving investment opportunity is particularly crucial. Nvidia's long-term competitive advantages remain substantial, but its valuation must be weighed against greater regulatory uncertainty and the possibility of slower industry growth. Until there is greater clarity surrounding the reported SEC investigation and signs of stabilization across semiconductor stocks, investors should remain cautious about assuming the recent sell-off has created a definitive buying opportunity.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that atmos Rewards is the airline loyalty program for Alaska Airlines and Hawaiian Airlines. One of its newer features is Atmos Communities, which offer additional rewards and benefits tailored to different travel interests.

    There are six communities, including two reserved for Alaska and Hawaii residents. The other four are open to members regardless of where they live. But don’t get caught up in the community names. The best choice for you may depend more on your travel plans than the groupings suggest.

    Here’s how to decide which Atmos Community best fits your travel patterns.

    » Learn more: The guide to Atmos Rewards.

    Atmos Communities are like groups within the Atmos Rewards program that offer additional benefits based on different travel interests.

    They’re free to join for Atmos Rewards members. Four communities are available to all members, while community Club 49 is reserved for Alaska residents and community Huaka’i by Hawaiian is reserved for Hawaii residents.

    According to recent reports, you can belong to only one community at a time and switch communities once per calendar year. Consider your upcoming travel plans before choosing.

    Each Atmos Community has a list of 10 destinations where members can earn bonus points and status points. Although the destinations differ by community, the rewards structure is the same.

    In a recent development, through Dec. 31, 2027, members can earn up to 10,000 bonus points and 10,000 status points by visiting qualifying destinations.

    Here’s how many points you’ll earn as you reach each milestone:.

    Visit one destination, earn 100 status and bonus points.

    Visit two destinations, earn 200 status and bonus points.

    Visit three destinations, earn 300 status and bonus points.

    Visit four destinations, earn 400 status and bonus points.

    Visit five destinations, earn 500 status and bonus points.

    Visit six destinations, earn 750 status and bonus points.

    Visit seven destinations, earn 1,000 status and bonus points.

    Visit eight destinations, earn 1,250 status and bonus points.

    Visit nine destinations, earn 2,500 status and bonus points.

    Visit 10 destinations, earn 3,000 status and bonus points.

    The first member of each community to visit all 10 qualifying destinations during the challenge period will also earn 100,000 bonus points.

    New lists of qualifying destinations for each community take effect on Jan. 1, 2028.

    Here’s a closer look at the six communities, their benefits and the destinations eligible for bonus points.

    Global Locals is geared toward frequent international travelers. Benefits include:.

    Earn 10% more status points toward Atmos elite status on flights that begin and/or end outside the U.S., including award flights.

    Earn 1 status point for every 25 points transferred to Atmos Rewards from Bilt or Marriott Bonvoy.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Industry observers note that through Dec. 31, 2027, these 10 Oneworld Alliance hubs count toward bonus points and status points. Qualifying layovers also count toward the destination challenge, so you don’t necessarily need to make these cities your final stop.

    If you frequently travel internationally or have any upcoming flights through any of these airports, including qualifying layovers, Global Locals might be a fit for you.

    Sources indicate that if you have the Atmos™ Rewards Summit Visa Infinite® credit card, you’ll earn 3 Atmos points per $1 spent on eligible Alaska and Hawaiian Airlines purchases, dining and foreign transactions. The last bonus category can be especially useful for frequent international travelers.

    Industry observers note that this community has a similar setup to Global Locals, but most of its bonus destinations are in the U.S. Here’s what you can get:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Sources indicate that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    This community would be an excellent choice if your upcoming travels include several of these airports, even if dining isn't the main reason for your trips. If dining out is one of your favorite activities, check out the best credit cards for restaurants.

    Recent findings suggest that active Escapes focuses on airports in outdoor-oriented destinations that are all in the U.S., save one. Benefits here are:.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus:.

    Industry observers note that while these airports are gateways to national parks and other natural attractions, you don’t have to be an outdoor enthusiast to benefit. Like before, don’t let the heading sway you. Rather, consider the destinations before you decide.

    Families On the Go might appeal to you if you redeem Atmos Rewards for your children. Benefits include:.

    Get 20% of your points back on eligible award flights for kids 12 and under after you complete your trip.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Recent findings suggest that through Dec. 31, 2027, these destinations qualify for bonus points and status points:.

    This community may be especially valuable if you regularly book award flights for children 12 and under. Even if you don't travel with kids, it could be worth considering if its qualifying airports align better with your travel plans than those of other communities.

    Exclusively for Alaska residents, Club 49 offers rewards that are focused on travel to, from and within the state:.

    Two free checked bags when traveling to or from Alaska on Alaska Airlines or Hawaiian Airlines.

    Three free checked bags when traveling within Alaska on Alaska Airlines.

    Two Travel Now discounts per year for 30% off one-way refundable Y-class fares on Alaska Airlines, booked within four days of departure for travel to, from or within Alaska.

    Ship cargo within Alaska for $49 plus tax (weight, size and content limits apply).

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    Recent findings suggest that baggage benefits don’t combine with other free checked bag allowances, such as those that come with some Alaska credit cards. However, they apply to everyone traveling on the same reservation.

    Recent findings suggest that through Dec. 31, 2027, here are the 10 destinations that count toward the bonus offers:.

    Recent findings suggest that while this community is only for Alaskans, you might decide one of the other communities more closely matches your travel intends — especially if you already have an Alaska credit card with free baggage benefits. However, if you ship a lot of cargo or think you’ll use the Travel Now discounts, those are special benefits that may sway you to choose Club 49.

    It has been revealed that hawaii residents have their own community just for them: Huaka’i by Hawaiian. It offers benefits focused on interisland travel:.

    Two free checked bags on neighbor island flights on Hawaiian Airlines, including sports equipment like surfboards and golf bags.

    Quarterly fare discounts of 10% off one neighbor island booking, or 20% off for eligible Hawaiian Airlines® World Elite Mastercard® and Atmos™ Rewards Visa® cardholders.

    Earn 50% more points and status points on flights between Hawaiian islands beginning Jan. 1, 2027.

    Get 20% off Atmos Rewards Unlocked experiences.

    It has been revealed that seven destinations are in Hawaii, with one on the mainland and two international cities. If you live in Hawaii and like to hop between islands, this community is a strong choice.

    Don’t be persuaded by the names of the communities. Look a little deeper, because there’s a lot of overlap between destination lists. Compare the options against your upcoming travel plans.

    It has been revealed that you can change communities once per calendar year, so you aren’t locked in to your initial choice indefinitely. However, switching communities resets your destination-challenge progress, but you’ll retain any points you’ve already earned.

    According to recent reports, if your home airport (or one you visit frequently) is already on a community’s list, you may have an easier time earning points. Also consider whether a particular community benefit, such as free checked bags or points back on award flights for kids, outweighs the destination challenge.

    Recent findings suggest that finally, pay attention to airport codes. For example, Tokyo’s Narita (NRT) and Haneda (HND) appear on different community lists. Upcoming York’s qualifying airport is JFK, while it is DCA in Washington, D.C. If you have a choice between airports, check which one qualifies for your community’s challenge.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.
    • At one point in 2025, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) fell 19% below its high.
    • In 2020, the index dropped by nearly 35% during the COVID pandemic.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By David Dierking – Nov 20, 2026 at 4:45PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Vanguard S&P 500 ETF ›.

    At one point in 2025, the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) fell 19% below its high. It still finished the year up 16%.

    In 2020, the index dropped by nearly 35% during the COVID pandemic. It also closed out the full calendar year with a gain of 16%.

    Industry observers note that in 2026, stocks are sliding again. Right now, the S&P 500 sits about 6% below its all-time high, but the Nasdaq-100 is down nearly 13%.

    Industry observers note that I don't tell you this to suggest that U.S. stocks are poised for a rapid recovery like they experienced earlier this decade. It's to tell you that episodes like this are part of the experience when investing in stocks.

    If you own the Vanguard S&P 500 ETF (VOO -3.42%), here's the one thing I'd tell you right now. These declines are no doubt painful, but they're the price of admission when accumulating long-term wealth.

    Here's an interesting bit of stock market trivia. Since 1980, the average intra-year drop in the S&P 500 has been 14.2%. But despite this, the S&P 500 has produced a positive calendar-year return in 35 of those 46 years.

    In other words, market corrections are a normal and regular occurrence for the S&P 500. But so are the recoveries from them. And the fact remains that stocks spend much more time rising than they do falling. The short-term losses are part of the path to long-term gains.

    One of the most underrated moves an investor can make is making no move at all.

    When stock prices are falling, many people rush to sell their stocks, fearing that more losses are on the way. They may say something like they're going to wait for things to get "better" before they get back in.

    There are a couple of things wrong with that thinking.

    First, selling stocks after they've fallen only locks in the loss. It doesn't erase it. Second, stock market rebounds are often well underway by the time investors feel that things have gotten "better.".

    In a recent development, the sum total of these actions means that a lot of folks lock in the loss, miss out on the rebound, and end up damaging their long-term returns. If the S&P 500's long-term annualized return is around 10%, the average investor usually ends up getting less than that.

    Recent findings suggest that that's why the one thing I like to tell investors is: Get used to the stock market's volatility. It's normal and it's a daily occurrence. Corrections of 10% or more are fairly frequent and should be expected from time to time. It's how you handle them that makes the difference. If you can buy and hold instead of giving in to the temptation to sell, you have a better chance of reaching your financial goals.
